articles.title: The ‘moon landing’ of gaming: Australians, some of the first to play GTA VI, prepare to descend on Vice City
articles.summary:
After a 13 year wait for the latest Grand Theft Auto instalment, Thursday’s launch is shaping up to be ‘the biggest gaming event that’s ever been’

Gamers across Australia are preparing for…

blocks.text: Gamers across Australia are preparing for the once-in-a-generation release of Grand Theft Auto VI, a day acolytes of the franchise say will be bigger than the biggest sporting events.

Details surrounding GTA VI, set in the fictional world of Leonida and its metropolis, the Miami-esque Vice City, have been scarce. But Rockstar Games has been building hype for months, driving supercars along Florida streets, planning a music festival and drip-feeding clips to a ravenous public.
With a global release time of the stroke of midnight on Thursday 19 November, Australians will be able to access the game second only to New Zealanders.
Joe Randle, an online creator known as ToastedShoes, said the game’s release was an unprecedented moment for the industry.
“It is by far the biggest gaming event that’s ever been,” he told Guardian Australia. “It’s not like the Super Bowl, that happens every year. I would probably call it the moon landing of gaming.”

Like other streamers, Randle will go live on Twitch just before the game drops and stream for hours into the night, with videos set to drop on YouTube shortly afterwards. Business aside, the release is an “incredibly exciting” time to be a fan.
“It’s a little bit surreal almost, like it’s too good to be true” he said. “I’ve waited years for this.”

The scale of the release is staggering. Rockstar hasn’t released any public figures, but it’s thought the game cost upwards of $1.5bn to develop. Estimates for preorders are approaching 16m copies, meaning the game has already brought in more than $2.2bn in revenue before its launch.

Analysts say that number could jump to $4.5bn to $7.5bn in its first week and keep climbing, figures that are even more stunning considering the game’s age restrictions: It’s rated 17+ in the US and R18+ in Australia, meaning it’s legally restricted to adults aged 18 and over.
NBN Co, the federal enterprise that operates the country’s broadband system, said data suggested Thursday will be a massive moment for Australian gamers.

Last Thursday, the first day people could pre-download the GTA VI, saw a new record set for the level of traffic on the NBN network. Every second, the equivalent of 57 days of full HD streaming video flowed through the NBN, about 10% higher than average.
In total, NBN said the excess data amounted to about 330,000 downloads of GTA VI since the preload period began.

Matt Judge, an Australian streamer with nearly a million Twitch followers under the handle DarkViperAU, has built a career within the world of Grand Theft Auto 5. The game came out in 2013, and in the intervening years Judge has spent more than 13,000 hours in the fictional world of Los Santos, based on Los Angeles.
GTA VI has promised to build on the good will Rockstar has cultivated with the franchise and beloved games such as the Red Dead Redemption series, he said.

“Waiting that long for anything obviously is going to build a lot of anticipation and hype,” Judge said, saying he has been adjusting his sleep schedule to get ready for a playing marathon, shifting his wake-up time from around 8.30am to 3.30pm. “There was some expectation that the game would be released in 2018, it’s not only that we’ve waited 13 years but we’ve waited eight years longer than we expected.”
As a fan, Judge can’t wait to immerse himself in the world of GTA VI. But as a creator, he’s a little daunted.

“A lot of what made me be successful online was my immense knowledge of the single player version of GTA V,” he said. “But now I’m starting on the ground floor with everyone else in a new world that I don’t know as well … that makes me a bit nervous.
“Everyone recognises that a new hit game could be your meal ticket.”

Maggie Brennan, a tattoo artist from Victoria who streams under the handle retromaggie, said the impending release feels like the drop of the year’s biggest action movie, paired with a major musical release. A 34-song soundtrack comes out on Friday.

“As a big fan of the GTA series, tomorrow’s game release is really exciting for myself and other gamers who have loved the worlds that Rockstar games have created,” she wrote in an email, adding the community surrounding the game had helped her deal with her own personal health struggles.

articles.title: Shaken and stirred: Jeff Bezos says he was ‘heavily involved’ in picking new James Bond
articles.summary:
Amazon’s executive chair and billionaire founder said he felt there was ‘something special’ about Robert Pattinson

Amazon’s founder and billionaire chairman

blocks.text: Amazon’s founder and billionaire chairman Jeff Bezos has said he was “heavily involved” in the decision to cast Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond.

Amazon paid more than $1bn for “creative control” of the Bond franchise last year, striking a deal with the longtime heirs and stewards of the films, shocking fans who worried that Bezos’ takeover would signal an end to the franchise as they knew it.
Bezos said he felt there was “something special” about Pattinson, revealing during an appearance at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World event that he reviewed several rounds of auditions.

blocks.caption: Piccadilly Circus screen displays announcement of Robert Pattinson as the next James Bond. Photograph: Felix Ursell/Reuters

blocks.text: “There was a big group initially, and we down-selected to five finalists. We did real, old-fashioned screen tests of those five finalists,” he said. “We did three different scenes with each of the five finalists, and then we got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all the tests and reviewing all that.”

He added that he and the film’s director, Dune’s Denis Villeneuve, were initially biased against Pattinson, seeking an unknown talent. “But in the screen tests, it was so obvious he is James Bond,” he said.
Pattinson, 40, made his big-screen debut in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire ⁠in 2005 and has gone on to star in ​films including The Twilight ​Saga, The Lost City of ​Z and Tenet.

Bezos’ Amazon acquired the MGM studio in an $8.5bn purchase in 2022. Bond fans and film critics have speculated over where Amazon will take the Bond franchise, with industry experts speculating the company may seek to expand the films into a Marvel-style universe of spinoffs.

Amazon has grown into a massive conglomerate in recent years, which includes not only an entertainment arm, but also computing and the company’s original business of online sales. Bezos also separately founded the space exploration company Blue Origin.

Amazon’s surveillance technology has come under criticism as a Guardian investigation this week unveiled that Israel was using its facial recognition tool to surveil Palestinians as part of a larger project to move its data on to Amazon servers.

articles.title: Asean adopts landmark declaration on space cooperation
articles.summary: MANILA, Philippines — Southeast Asian leaders have adopted the region’s first declaration dedicated exclusively to space cooperation, setting out common priorities for collaboration in space safety…

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Southeast Asian leaders have adopted the region’s first declaration dedicated exclusively to space cooperation, setting out common priorities for collaboration in space safety and security, the space economy and workforce development.

The Asean Leaders’ Declaration on the Advancement of Space Science, Technology and Innovation Cooperation was adopted Nov. 15 during the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations Summit in Manila, the Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA) said in a statement Tuesday.

The declaration was spearheaded by the Philippines through PhilSA, the country’s national focal point for space matters under the Asean Subcommittee on Earth, Ocean and Space Science, and the Department of Science and Technology (DOST), which chairs the Asean Committee on Science, Technology and Innovation.

PhilSA said the declaration was among the priority economic deliverables of the Philippines’ Asean chairship. It seeks to establish a common framework for regional cooperation and encourage the joint use of space technologies among member states.

“More than a formal statement, this Declaration reflects a shared regional vision to strengthen collaboration in space science, technology, and innovation. Through this, we hope to further advance Asean’s collective capacity to harness space technologies in support of disaster resilience, environmental sustainability, economic growth, and inclusive development across our region,” PhilSA Director General Gay Jane Perez said.

The declaration identifies three areas for stronger cooperation: space security and safety, the space economy and space workforce development. It also promotes joint research, capacity-building activities and the sharing of space infrastructure and data.
Regional cooperation
According to PhilSA, the agreement builds on several activities organized by the Philippines during its Asean chairship to encourage regional collaboration in space science and technology.

On March 12 and 13, PhilSA, in partnership with the United Nations Office for Outer Space Affairs and Thailand’s Geo-Informatics and Space Technology Development Agency, held a seminar-workshop in Manila on space situational awareness and space traffic management.
The event brought together Asean representatives, policymakers, technical experts and commercial operators to discuss regional approaches to space safety, data sharing and operational coordination.

PhilSA also organized the Asean Space Forum: Navigating Our Future through Space Diplomacy during Philippine Space Week 2026 to discuss the proposed declaration, build partnerships and explore opportunities for regional cooperation in the global space sector.
Space economy
The potential of space technology for business and economic development was also discussed during the Asean Business and Investment Summit 2026 in Pasay City on Nov. 15.

In a keynote address, Japanese astronaut and Axiom Space chief technology officer for Asia Pacific Dr. Koichi Wakata discussed opportunities for the Philippines and other Asean countries in space research, advanced manufacturing and human spaceflight as commercial access to orbit expands.
A panel discussion titled “Space Economy: Asean’s Next Frontier” also explored how space technology could create business opportunities and contribute to everyday life across Southeast Asia.

Moderated by PhilSA founding Director General and University of the Philippines Vice President for Research and Innovation Dr. Joel Joseph Marciano Jr., the panel included Wakata, Hidetaka Aoki of Space Port Japan, Christian Patouraux of Kacific, Robbie Schingler of Planet and Ramon Garcia Jr. of Ascend International Gateway.

The discussion covered opportunities across the space industry, including satellite manufacturing, ground infrastructure, data analytics, connectivity and commercial applications. It also examined how Asean could develop a competitive and sustainable regional space economy.
To further explore opportunities for the Philippine space sector, PhilSA will hold Space Partnerships, Acceleration, Research, Commercialization and Synergies (SPARCS) 2026 on Nov. 23.

The event will gather representatives from government, industry, academe, startups, investment and research institutions, and development partners. Discussions will cover ways to strengthen the country’s capabilities in space manufacturing, spaceport and commercial launch services, and the development of applications and services using space technology.
Next steps
PhilSA is also set to hold a virtual ceremonial launch of the Asean Declaration on Space Cooperation and a forum on Dec. 7 under the theme “Navigating Asean’s Future in Space, Together.”

The event will bring together representatives from Asean member states, dialogue partners and other stakeholders to discuss the declaration’s provisions and identify opportunities to translate its commitments into regional initiatives.

“The adoption reaffirms Asean’s shared commitment to harnessing space science, technology, and innovation for sustainable development, regional resilience, and a more connected and collaborative space community,” PhilSA said in a statement. /dm

articles.title: Sleeve checks and no smartglasses: South Korea races to protect all-important university exams against AI
articles.summary:
South Korea has been gripped by revelations of AI-aided cheating, just days before more than half a million students are to sit high-stakes entrance exams

The integrity of South Korea’s…

blocks.text: The integrity of South Korea’s career-defining university entrance exam has been thrown into doubt after the top scorer in a recent professional exam admitted using a concealed camera and AI to cheat.

On Thursday, more than half a million people, mostly school students, are due to sit the exam, known as the suneung, at 1,312 centres across the country. The exam runs for a gruelling eight hours over a single day and determines which university a candidate can attend and, in turn, their future prospects.

The country goes to great lengths to ensure the smooth running of the suneung. Aircraft take-offs and landings are rescheduled during the 25-minute English listening paper to minimise noise, while artillery fire and tank movements are suspended.

The stock market opens an hour late and cars are stopped 200 metres from every centre. Extra trains run from 6am, police drive latecomers to their exam halls, and tourist attractions open late to ease traffic. Offices are asked to open at 10am.

But in recent days, exam organisers have faced a renewed threat to the validity of the entire exercise, after the top scorer in this year’s tax accountancy exam- who got just one question wrong out of 160– admitted on Sunday he had cheated by using AI.
Prime minister Han Seong-sook told a cabinet meeting in Seoul on Tuesday that AI-assisted cheating was a “social evil” that the government would “root out”.
“We will block outright the carrying of smart devices during the exam,” she said. The education ministry and other agencies should approach it “as if staking their jobs on it”, she added.

Han said smart devices must be turned off and handed in, while bags left in corridors would be checked for any devices that were still on. Exam officials would also inspect all candidates’ glasses and watches, as well as their collars, sleeves and buttons for concealed cameras.
The government will also send emergency alerts to every phone in the country, which sound at full volume and cannot be silenced, in the hope of catching out anyone who has not handed in their device.

More invigilators will be deployed, and the government said it was preparing to switch off school wifi inside exam centres and public wifi nearby, and that personal hotspots, which cannot be blocked, would be traced through connection records.
The weekend’s cheating revelation captured national headlines in South Korea, stoking concern about the security of the suneung.

In a video posted to his lawyer’s YouTube channel, the exam cheat said he had photographed the questions with a concealed microcamera, sent them to an AI system and read the answers from a smartphone. “I cheated in the tax accountant exam,” he said. “My top placing is not the result of legitimate effort.”

blocks.caption: South Korean education minister Choi Kyo-jin reviews the method used to cheat in the national tax accountant exam. Photograph: Seo Dae-yeon/YONHAP/AP

blocks.text: His lawyer handed police a camera, a laptop and a phone. No charges have been brought, and the prime minister has ordered procedures to begin that would void his result and bar him for five years.

The education minister, Choi Kyo-jin, told parliament on Monday that while authorities could screen out the smart glasses already on sale at Thursday’s exam, newer variants could not be dealt with perfectly.

Choi has ruled out postponing the exam, which has been delayed several times before, including in 2017, after an earthquake struck the south-eastern city of Pohang, and in 2020 due to the Covid pandemic.

Smart glasses have been banned in exams since the end of June. In October, several candidates were caught with them while sitting university-run admissions exams. At the suneung, wearing a pair counts as using one even when switched off.

The education ministry looked at using radio-frequency equipment to detect the glasses in exam halls, but concluded conditions varied too much between venues for deployment this year. Checks will instead rely on visual inspection, with at least one dedicated official placed in each exam centre.

blocks.caption: Workers process packages of question-and-answer sheets for South Korea’s university entrance exams on 16 November. Photograph: YONHAP/EPA

blocks.text: Teachers’ unions have criticised the government response as belated. A survey last month of 2,716 secondary school teachers by the Korean Teachers and Education Workers Union showed that 82.3% said they could not tell whether a candidate was wearing smart glasses under the current procedure, with only 3.5% saying they could.

To avoid facing scrutiny on exam day, some candidates are reportedly switching to contact lenses. An optician in Suwon, south of Seoul, said students who had never worn contacts were coming in to ask how to put them in.
Han said on X on Monday that the checks would be handled carefully “so that candidates acting in good faith do not suffer unnecessary anxiety or inconvenience”.
In his video confession, the accountancy test cheat addressed suneung candidates directly. “The suneung is coming up soon,” he said.
“To anyone thinking of cheating as I did: I am going to tell the investigators everything, so please don’t think, ‘I won’t get caught.’”

articles.title: Would AI have come up with a better word of the year than the Cambridge Dictionary?
articles.summary: The Cambridge Dictionary has chosen "human" as its word of the year, reflecting concerns about artificial intelligence.

image.caption: The Cambridge Dictionary has chosen 'human' as its 2026 word of the year. (Nathan Howard/Reuters)

blocks.text: World·New
The Cambridge Dictionary has chosen "human" as its word of the year, reflecting concerns about artificial intelligence.
The publication has chosen 'human' in response to concerns around artificial intelligence
The choice announced Wednesday in the U.K. highlights the debate over how AI blurs the lines between machines and people.

Explaining the choice, the dictionary said, "Throughout history, the adjective human has signified people, as opposed to animals and gods (and, more recently, machines). Increasingly seen in compounds such as human-written, human-generated, and human-made, it now also denotes that something is created by or typical of people as opposed to AI."

Colin McIntosh, the dictionary's lexicographer, notes that though AI has been a growing presence in society for years, in 2026, it seemed to be everywhere — and changed how people talk about being human.

"2026 has been all about a refound appreciation of the human factor in what we consume (with a consequent human premium)," he said in a statement, "and a new value is being placed on the human element in our lives in general: all confirmed by our analysis of the language data, internet trends, and search habits."
Given that, he said, human was the perfect choice.
He used Meta’s AI agent Muse for Marketplace sales. Then it set one up behind his back

Last year's word of the year was also AI-related. Cambridge Dictionary chose "parasocial," explaining that "as social media intensifies the intimacy that fans feel with their adored celebrities, and with the rise in popularity of AI companions that can take on personalities, the word for these one-way relationships — parasocial — is having its own moment."
Four other words made the shortlist for the 2026 word of the year: analogue, agent, wholesome and chic.
With files from CBC News

articles.title: How populist parties around the world use the same playbook to win on social media
articles.summary: Here are the four basic moves in the “social media playbook” shared by many populist parties

items: Politicians now directly engage with voters through social media, bypassing traditional media gatekeepers, which has benefited populist leaders globally.
A social media playbook used by populist parties includes four key strategies: building an audience, provoking them, encouraging message spreading, and listening to feedback.

The rise of populism is facilitated by social media's engagement algorithms, which amplify simplistic messaging and can be enhanced by AI tools, making it challenging for mainstream parties to compete.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

Not too long ago, when politicians wanted to reach the public they had to get past journalists, editors and producers, who collectively decided what made the news. But now, politicians can post, livestream, and message voters directly on social media platforms.
On platforms such as Instagram, Tiktok and YouTube, engagement algorithms designed to hold viewers’ attention determine what voters see and how often.
The shift to algorithmic social media has been great for populist politicians around the world, who position themselves as representing the “will of the people”.

In our recent research (under peer review), we collected 35,500 public posts from TikTok, Instagram, Facebook and YouTube, posted during elections by parties and politicians across the political spectrum in several countries.
Based on our analysis of this data, we found the “social media playbook” shared by many populist parties has four basic moves:

items: build an audience
provoke the audience
encourage the audience to spread the message
listen to the audience and give them more of what they want.

blocks.text: These moves use the rules of social media platforms to gain attention, support and votes.
Populism is a word that gets thrown around a lot, and is often used as a euphemism for the far right.
On a more careful view, the defining feature of populism is it splits society into “the pure people” and “the corrupt elite”. It holds that politics should express the “general will” of the people.
Populism is a thin ideology that can come from the left or the right. It can be combined with fuller ideologies from nationalism to socialism.
Social media fits well with populism, as it gives populists a channel to invoke the support of people against the establishment.
Populists across the globe have made the most of social media. In Argentina, the rise of Javier Milei to the presidency in 2023 is partly attributed to his TikTok account of 1.5 million followers.
In Germany, two populist parties, both with a highly visible TikTok presence, doubled their vote at the 2025 election.

In New York, Zohran Mamdani rose from 1% in early polls to mayor in 2025, helped by short videos on TikTok and Instagram. In the United Kingdom, Nigel Farage entered Parliament in 2024 with more than 800,000 highly engaged TikTok followers.

And in Australia, One Nation, dismissed for decades as a fringe party, has polled 24-31% on primary votes this year. Its rise has been accompanied by cartoons and AI-generated ads with millions of views on social media.
These parties and leaders differ sharply in politics, but their methods are remarkably alike.
Our research found a social media playbook of four moves: build, provoke, spread, listen.

The first move is to “build” audiences across several platforms, using free accounts, follower networks and livestreaming. The leader is the brand, and short-form videos filmed with front-facing cameras project apparent authenticity. Building may also involve values-based content that makes the party seem reasonable and relatable.

The second move is to “provoke” by simplifying issues, finding people to blame, and getting headlines. Short posts in simple language will make bold claims about complex problems such as housing or cost of living. Often the “corrupt elite”, the media or outsiders are blamed. Part of the goal here is to push the stories from social media into mainstream news.

The third move is to “spread” the message via followers. Share buttons, comment threads and tools such as TikTok’s duet and stitch make every follower a potential broadcaster. The platform’s engagement algorithms will then push the message to new audiences.
Finally, “listen” uses audience engagement as live opinion polling. Platform analytics show which posts land within minutes, and ad tools can test different versions of a message.
Whatever draws the most reactions becomes the next message, or even the next policy.

Artificial intelligence (AI) is a big part of the playbook. The platform engagement algorithms are a kind of AI, and generative AI tools for producing text, images and video make all the moves cheaper and faster. A single video can be cut, captioned and translated for diverse demographics, and millions of likes, comments, views sorted by mood for targeted campaigns in minutes.

An adversary can be made vivid with a synthetic image, as One Nation’s AI-made Victorian election ad shows. AI agents can even run accounts that post, reply and share around the clock, making a few supporters look like many.

Mainstream parties struggle with copying these moves because complex policies don’t fit into 15-second clips, and sound scripted beside a leader talking straight to the camera. Also, parties chasing broad support may avoid sharp messages that rally one group but alienate another.

Platforms profit from this populist playbook, as their algorithms amplify the kind of messaging that keeps people scrolling and drives advertising revenue. Attempts to make platforms offer a simpler, chronological feed of posts – such as the Australian government’s “My Feed, My Way” bill – would weaken part of this approach, but most of it would still work.
That is why media literacy matters now and into the future, especially as AI blurs what’s real.

This populist approach works by getting people to play along. So next time you see a post that makes you angry or hands you a villain, pause for a moment. Ask who made it, why, and what has been left out. You might have to look up some other credible sources on the topic – not just asking a chatbot – and gain a broader knowledge.
Engagement algorithms are trained on our reactions. The most effective thing you can do is to stop and think before you hit share. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Tag team: dual waterspouts appear in San Francisco Bay amid stormy weather
articles.summary:
Phenomenon is not a common occurrence in the Bay area and inclement weather is expected to continue for few days

A pair of waterspouts were recorded recently in the San Francisco Bay area,…

blocks.text: A pair of waterspouts were recorded recently in the San Francisco Bay area, much to the delight and shock of several observers, as storms pummelled the region.

Two waterspouts – vortexes of air and water mist, essentially tornadoes – cut a sheer streak into the sky, as they spiraled above the bay, according to social media footage capturing the weather phenomenon.
While prevalent in the Great Lakes and the south-east Floridian coast, waterspout sightings are not common for the Bay area, according to federal storm data.

The National Weather Service (NWS) confirmed the waterspout occurrence in a Monday special marine warning. Some waterspouts, dubbed “fair weather”, are weak, while others, typically tornadic waterspouts can pose a risk to boaters and coastal areas if they travel on shore.

The inclement weather is set to continue for a few more days. According to an NWS forecast, the Bay area is predicted to be drenched in rain on Tuesday with potential thunderstorms on Wednesday and Thursday.
Elevated tide levels raise the risk of coastal flooding through at least Thursday, according to the agency.
Powerful wind is also forecasted with East Bay Hills expected to see gusts reaching up to 70mph (112 km/h).
After Thursday evening, the showers may subside with some rain lingering over the Pacific and its adjacent inland communities.

The camp of Vice President Sara Duterte said Wednesday that her two former staff who sought help due to alleged threats to their lives are now safe and sound.
In a post on Facebook, Atty. Salvador Paolo Panelo, Duterte's spokesperson, said they were able to rescue the two with the help of the police on Tuesday.

"Yesterday (November 17, 2026), the Vice President’s legal team, with police assistance, fetched them and brought them to a police station where they executed affidavits and filed a police blotter," he said.
"For now, the apparent plan to use these individuals for false testimony against the Vice President has been foiled," he added.

He said the two were recruited and engaged by a private individual to work as employees at a resort in Boracay sometime in October. They were then brought to Manila under the pretext of training for their roles.
Panelo said that on November 16, the supposed employer informed the two of the threats to their lives, and that there was also a threat to the employer’s own life because he was “harboring” them.

"The employer then told them that the threats would be quelled if they executed affidavits, drafts of which were presented to them. According to the two individuals, the affidavits contained false allegations against the Vice President, which they refused to sign," he added.
He further said that later that day, one of them reached out to the Vice President for "assistance to extricate themselves from the situation and for safe passage."
Panelo said the two clarified that they were not held in captivity, but they were afraid to leave the employer’s custody due to the supposed threat to their lives.
He said that, for the safety of those involved, they will not provide any further details about the matter.
Malacañang on Tuesday called for an investigation into the claims.

The National Bureau of Investigation, Philippine National Police, and House impeachment trial spokesperson Lanao del Sur Rep. Zia Alonto Adiong, meanwhile, urged Duterte's camp to file a formal report over the alleged threats. —AOL, GMA News

items: The National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) filed a motion for the release of 216 individuals detained for over 36 hours after a mass arrest during a protest in Muntinlupa City.
NUPL argues that the detainees have not received any formal charges or evidence against them, violating their rights under Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code.

MANILA, Philippines – The National Union of Peoples’ Lawyers (NUPL) on Tuesday, November 17, filed a motion with the Muntinlupa City Prosecutor’s Office seeking the release of 216 people who have been detained for more than 36 hours following a mass arrest in Muntinlupa City.
In its motion, NUPL said those detained have yet to receive copies of any complaint-affidavit, witness affidavits, or other evidence supporting the charges against them.
Article 125 of the Revised Penal Code requires authorities to bring persons arrested without a warrant before judicial authorities within 12, 18, or 36 hours, depending on the gravity of the offense.
“The prolonged detention of the Respondents, absent the filing of a criminal case, constitutes a continuing violation of their fundamental rights,” NUPL said.

The lawyers asserted that the arrested individuals had not committed any criminal offense, saying many were merely exercising their constitutional rights to free speech, peaceful assembly, and to seek redress of grievances.
The individuals were arrested during a Pax Silica protest on the opening day of the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila on Sunday, November 15. They are detained at Camp Bagong Diwa in Taguig City.
There are also minors who were arrested and brought to Bahay Pag-asa Tunasan, Muntinlupa.

The protesters, mostly members of Lakbayan Timog Katagalugan, were heading to Liwasang Bonifacio to join other groups opposing Pax Silica and US President Donald Trump’s scheduled arrival in the country.
Trump arrived on Tuesday, November 17, for the ASEAN-US Special Summit and a state visit.
At Liwasang Bonifacio, police arrested another 11 people as tensions rose between officers and protesters.
Several groups questioned the massive arrest and called for the release of those arrested.

University of the Philippines Diliman’s Council Committee on National Programs and Policies urged the Philippine National Police to release those who detained. In a statement on Tuesday, UP said protesters who gathered in their campus were prevented by the police to join the protest in Manila.

“Contrary to its initial recommendation that mass actions be done only after the 49th ASEAN Summit and other related summits, the government should allow ongoing protests to continue. These are not sources of embarrassment as these show openness to opposing views and the tolerance of critical reportage,” UP said. – Rappler.com

Police on Wednesday tightened security along roads leading to Malacañang in Mendiola, Manila and around a hotel in Parañaque where foreign delegates to the ASEAN Summit 2026 stayed.
Protesters continued to conduct activities against the visit of United States President Donald Trump in the Philippines.

In Manila, police set up barricades along Recto Avenue corner San Sebastian Street near Mendiola, blocking both lanes with barbed wire and three container vans, according to James Agustin's report on GMA News’ Unang Balita.
Legarda Street corner Figueras Street was also closed to motorists, while both lanes of Ayala Bridge were blocked, forcing motorists to take alternative routes.
Road closures affected commuters and transport workers. Some passengers had to walk after being dropped off near the barricades. Other motorists were also forced to take longer routes.
Police augmentation personnel from Police Regional Office 4A were positioned near Recto Avenue, while personnel from the National Capital Region Police Office (NCRPO) were deployed around Mendiola.
The heightened security came as various groups continued holding protests against Trump's visit to the Philippines for the ASEAN Summit.
In Parañaque, police maintained heightened security around Solaire Resort Entertainment City, where various foreign ASEAN delegations stayed overnight, GMA News’ Bam Alegre also reported.

The Southern Police District monitored the area through advanced command posts at Solaire and the Philippine International Convention Center (PICC), with police mobile units deployed at strategic locations.

Meanwhile, police continued to secure Liwasang Bonifacio as protesters including indigenous people concluded their three-day encampment, according to a report of GMA News’ Gabriel Gonzales on Unang Balita.
The Manila Police District (MPD) said 15 of the 22 people arrested in connection with protests since Sunday had already been charged.
Protesters had earlier attempted to proceed to Mendiola but police did not allow them to leave Liwasang Bonifacio.
The security measures are part of the interagency coordination following Trump's arrival in the Philippines on Tuesday for the ASEAN Summit 2026.

Trump is scheduled to go to Malacañang on Wednesday for a state visit with President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. The program includes arrival honors and a welcome ceremony at the Kalayaan Grounds at 11 a.m., followed by the signing of the guest book at 11:25 a.m. — Jamil Santos/RSJ, GMA News

articles.title: White House withdraws nomination of Heidi Overton to lead FDA
articles.summary:
Move to drop Trump ally and prominent abortion opponent comes a day before key Senate health committee vote

The White House has dropped its nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and…

blocks.text: The White House has dropped its nomination of Heidi Overton to lead the Food and Drug Administration, a White House official told the Guardian.

Donald Trump nominated Overton – a physician and prominent abortion opponent – in August. Overton has spent most of her professional career working directly for Trump or conservative groups aligned with his agenda. Her nomination in August was seen as a move to bring a stabilizing Trump loyalist to the agency after a tumultous year under Trump’s first FDA commissioner, Marty Makary.
But Overton faced bipartisan questions in the Senate about her willingness to break from Trump, particularly on his unsupported claims about the dangers of childhood vaccines.

Republican senator Bill Cassidy, a Louisiana doctor who chairs the Senate health committee, said earlier on Tuesday that he remained undecided about her nomination ahead of a Senate health, labor and pensions committee vote scheduled for Wednesday.

Cassidy had previously called Overton’s support for Trump’s plan to break up combination vaccines – including the measles, mumps and rubella shot – “almost disqualifying”. And he pressed her during a September hearing about her scientific independence and willingness to push back against Trump and health secretary Robert F Kennedy Jr, a longtime vaccine critic.
A prominent reproductive rights group celebrated the White House’s decision to withdraw Overton’s nomination.

Mini Timmaraju, the president and CEO of Reproductive Freedom for All, formerly Naral Pro-Choice America, said: “Heidi Overton posed a serious threat to the future of medication abortion access. Voters rejected that anti-abortion agenda nationwide, and our members kept the pressure on to tank her confirmation. If Republicans try to rush through another nominee who threatens our healthcare, we’re ready to keep fighting.”

As the head of the FDA, Overton would have overseen the agency that regulates medication abortions. In a 2023 policy brief for the conservative America First Policy Institute, Overton said Congress should strictly regulate the abortion pill mifeprestone “to protect women and children”, criticized federal policies that allow for the mailing of abortion pills and wrote that abortion “is corrosive to children, women, and society broadly”.

To win confirmation, Overton would have needed the votes of all 12 Republicans on the Senate health, education, labor and pensions committee. Democrats hold 11 seats. Without support of the committee, Overton faced little chance of winning a full Senate vote on chamber floor.
Republicans are racing to try to confirm all of Trump’s current nominees before they hand over power to Senate Democrats in January.

blocks.text: NEW BOND. The Piccadilly Circus screen displays an announcement that British actor Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond in an upcoming film from Amazon MGM Studios, in London, Britain, November 16, 2026.
via REUTERS
Amazon founder Jeff Bezos says it is clear there is 'something special' about Robert Pattinson
SAN FRANCISCO, USA – Amazon founder and chairman Jeff Bezos said he was heavily involved in selecting “Batman” actor Robert Pattinson to take on the iconic film role of James Bond.

Bezos spoke at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference on Tuesday, a day after the company announced Pattinson as the next 007. He said Amazon narrowed down a larger group and screen-tested five actors by having them perform three scenes in full costume on sets.
“I was heavily involved,” Bezos said. “We got together on Friday to spend a couple of hours looking at all the screening tests and reviewing all of that.”

The Bond franchise — about a British secret agent known for his charm, his tailored tuxedos and a fondness for martinis “shaken, not stirred” — is among the longest-running and highest-grossing in Hollywood history.
Bezos said it was clear there was “something special” about Pattinson.

“Initially, I would say we were slightly biased a little against him just because he’s already so famous,” Bezos said. “We sort of thought, you know, maybe we should have somebody a little more unknown. But in the screening tests, it was so obvious. He is James Bond.”
Pattinson, 40, made his big-screen debut in “Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire” in 2005 and has gone on to star in films such as “The Twilight Saga”, “The Lost City of Z” and “Tenet”.

More than two dozen Bond films have been released. The upcoming movie will be the first Bond adventure under Amazon MGM Studios, which took creative control of the film franchise under a new joint venture with longtime rights holders Michael Wilson and Barbara Broccoli in 2025. – Rappler.com

items: US President Donald Trump is set to meet Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on November 18 to discuss US security commitments amid rising tensions with China in the South China Sea.

Trump's Asia trip follows a challenging midterm election for Republicans and includes meetings with Quad leaders and a crucial meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping to address trade and economic relations.

The potential for a meeting with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un and discussions involving nuclear powers Xi and Putin may raise concerns among US allies regarding the implications of a US-China-Russia alliance.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.

MANILA, Philippines – US President Donald Trump will meet President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday, November 18, before heading to China for high-stakes talks with his Chinese and Russian counterparts, seeking to advance US interests in Asia while navigating tensions with Washington’s biggest strategic rival.

Trump’s meeting with Marcos at the presidential palace in Manila will give Marcos an opportunity to press for stronger US security commitments as China steps up its activities in the disputed South China Sea.
The two leaders are scheduled to hold bilateral talks and a working lunch before Trump departs for Shenzhen, in southern China.

blocks.caption: 49th ASEAN Summit closes, Philippines turns over chairmanship to Singapore

blocks.text: Trump arrived in Asia reeling from a bruising midterm election in which Republicans suffered sweeping defeats, raising questions about his domestic political standing. His meetings with regional leaders and, most consequentially, Chinese President Xi Jinping will test whether he can still project strength and wield leverage on the world stage.
On Tuesday, November 17, Trump kicked off his Asia trip with his first meeting with leaders of the Quad, the Indo-Pacific grouping of the United States, Japan, India and Australia.
That agenda included critical minerals that drive high-tech industries, maritime security, and artificial intelligence.
As the Quad leaders gathered, Trump told reporters that he wanted to ensure the future of AI was shaped by countries that shared US values.

The engagements will be closely watched for signs of Washington’s commitment to the Indo-Pacific, as allies seek reassurance about US security and economic engagement in a region where China remains a dominant trading partner.

For Marcos, one of Washington’s closest security partners in the region, the talks come amid growing friction with Beijing over competing claims in the South China Sea. The Philippines has sought clearer assurances about US willingness to defend Philippine forces and vessels in the disputed waters.

Trump will later travel to Shenzhen for Thursday’s meeting with Xi on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. The two leaders are expected to discuss trade and economic relations, with China’s restrictions on rare earth exports and US curbs on advanced semiconductor sales among the central issues.

Trump has also floated the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un, saying he had asked Xi to help arrange an encounter. No meeting has been confirmed, and North Korea has shown little interest in renewed diplomacy.
“He may come. I don’t know. That’s up to President Xi,” Trump told reporters before leaving Washington on Monday.

blocks.caption: Trump says he might meet with North Korea’s Kim Jong Un in China

blocks.text: Trump was expected to bring Elon Musk, the billionaire head of Tesla and SpaceX, to China, where his companies have significant commercial interests. Mastercard CEO Michael Miebach and FedEx CEO Raj Subramaniam were also expected at APEC-related events, according to people familiar with preparations.

Jensen Huang, who has been a regular participant in high-profile gatherings involving Trump and Asian leaders, is not expected to join the delegation after he resigned as Nvidia’s chief executive amid allegations that a woman with whom he had a relationship had ties to Chinese intelligence. Huang has denied wrongdoing. Trump said before leaving Washington that he would support Huang getting his job back.
The controversy adds sensitivity to discussions over US restrictions on advanced AI chips and China’s access to the technology.

Trump is also scheduled to take part in a trilateral meeting with Xi and Putin on Thursday, bringing together the leaders of three major nuclear powers. Trump has said the discussions could address nuclear arms control and Iran, while the war in Ukraine could also feature. Officials and analysts have played down the prospect of major agreements.
The meeting could unsettle US allies, who are watching Trump navigate ties with two of Washington’s biggest strategic rivals.

“His willingness to engage in this manner suggests an openness to the idea of a US-China-Russia ‘G3’,” said Oleg Ignatov, senior Russia analyst at the International Crisis Group. “His interest in such arrangements unnerves US allies and partners, who question how their interests will fare if these three powers try to manoeuvre around and above them.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: One Nation says it would cut Australia’s refugee intake by 90% under ‘tough stance’
articles.summary:
Pauline Hanson opens new war of words on immigration as foreign minister Penny Wong accuses populist party of ‘dividing Australians’

  • Get our

blocks.text: One Nation has vowed to cut Australia’s refugee intake by 90% and scrap the permanent parent visa program under its latest hardline plan to slash migration.
Pauline Hanson announced the policy on Tuesday labelling it a “tough” approach to migration.
The rightwing party said if it held power it would cut the refugee program from 20,000 places per year to 2,000 and claimed Australia would still remain above the OECD average for places per capita.
One Nation’s push would end Australia’s status as one of the most generous refugee programs behind Canada.
“The cost [to] … the taxpayer is enormous. The cost is, on average, about $500,000 a year in a lifetime of expenditure per person in the country,” Hanson told reporters.

“We’ve got to take a tough stance on this. My concern is for these people out there … that are doing it tough. You don’t bring more people into the country if they cannot fund their own bed or hospital beds.”

Hanson claimed her plan would save the budget more than $140bn over 10 years. Migrants from countries on the Albanese government’s “do not travel” list, including Iran, Lebanon, Syria and Somalia, would still be banned from entering the country.

One Nation says analysis based on Treasury modelling, adjusted for inflation, found the lifetime cost of a humanitarian entrant was $523,000. Treasury modelling done in December 2021 found the cost was $400,000 with 90% of it borne by the federal government.
Labor has committed to retaining the refugee intake at 20,000 per year while the Coalition has promised to halve it to 10,000.

The foreign minister, Penny Wong, accused One Nation of trying to divide the country. She said Australia had the right balance and questioned Hanson’s claim that Australia would remain above the OECD average under the minor party’s plan.

“I don’t accept those figures and I find when Ms Hanson speaks, you always have to check what is actually being said. There are countries which take more refugees, there are countries which take fewer. We think this [20,000 per year] is the right balance,” Wong said.

“We have unprecedented people movement around the world. We have displacement of more human beings than at any time since world war II. We make a very small contribution to that by our refugee intake.”
after newsletter promotion
Wong said it was “more of the same” from One Nation.
“I know that they think dividing Australians is the best response to the politics of the time,” the Labor frontbencher said. “I take a different view.”
Other nations including the US and Canada have tightened their migration programs in recent years with Canada reducing its parent visa program.
Hanson said One Nation was not barring migrant parents from moving to Australia, but they would have to be sponsored, or could visit their families on temporary visas.
“We’re not saying parents can’t come out … [but] they will actually be sponsored by the families not the taxpayers.”

articles.title: What Trump said and did in his first hours in Manila
articles.summary: The US president used his stop in manila to set the agenda for China and the Quad while reassuring Southeast Asian leaders.

blocks.text: November 18, 2026 | 8:36am

MANILA, Philippines — US President Donald Trump used a brief stop in Manila to rally Indo-Pacific partners around security, critical minerals and trade after arriving past 5:30 p.m. Tuesday, November 17.
Within hours of landing, Trump met fellow Quad leaders, signed a trade statement with Thailand and predicted that the United States would catch China in rare earths within 10 months.

He also floated possible meetings with Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during the next legs of his trip after Manila. He also signaled that Taiwan would likely come up in his talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Trump's Manila stop was the first leg of a three-day Asian trip. He is due to travel to Shenzhen for the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit after meeting President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on Wednesday.
Goes straight to Quad talks
Trump was welcomed by Executive Secretary Ralph Recto, Rep. Sandro Marcos (Ilocos Norte), Philippine Ambassador to the United States Jose Manuel Romualdez and US Ambassador Lee Lipton.

He then headed to Solaire Resort for talks with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi. The meeting was Trump's first with fellow Quad leaders since returning to the White House.
"Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific," Trump said.

US President Donald Trump, Australia's Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, India's Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi take part in a meeting of the Quad group—the United States, Japan, Australia and India—on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on Nov. 17, 2026.
AFP / Mandel Ngan
The four countries expressed concern over "economic coercion," including arbitrary export restrictions, without naming China.

They also unveiled new cooperation on maritime security and technology. The plans include a 2027 exercise involving P-8 and P-3C maritime patrol aircraft and continued work on an accelerator to coordinate and finance artificial-intelligence development across the Indo-Pacific.
The Quad plans to hold its first Business Leaders' Forum in 2027.
Mentions rare earths agenda
Trump's China agenda quickly dominated Trump's Manila appearances as he prepared to meet Xi, touting the progress in rare earths production that he claimed would catch China soon.
"We are making rare earths at a level that we've never made before. We're going to catch them within 10 months, they say," Trump told reporters.
China's lead in global rare-earth processing and supply chains gives Beijing leverage as trade tensions with Washington extend into critical minerals and advanced technology.
Trump said the Quad countries were increasing cooperation on minerals and rare earths to reduce dependence on a single supplier.
Floats Putin, Kim meetings
The US leader also raised the prospect of separate meetings with Putin and Kim in China.
Asked whether he would meet Putin during the APEC summit, Trump said: "If it's available, I would do that."
Trump suggested that Kim also wanted to attend. "He would like to, yes. We'll see what happens," he said.
Beijing earlier said it had no information about a possible meeting involving Kim.
Trump also expected Xi to raise Taiwan. "I'm sure he'll raise it. I won't have to raise it," he said.
Signs trade agreement with Thailand
Trump also signed a joint statement on reciprocal trade with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul that outlines proposed terms rather than a final agreement.

Thailand's Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul and US President Donald Trump take part in a signing of a US-Thailand trade agreement at the Solaire Resort on the sidelines of the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on Nov. 17, 2026.
Trump said the two sides were still negotiating and expected to complete a formal deal within weeks.

Under the proposed arrangement described by Trump, Thailand would eliminate tariffs on US exports and remove non-tariff barriers affecting American vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol and poultry.
Thailand would also buy an estimated $2.6 billion in additional US agricultural products, he said.
"It's going to be a wonderful deal for both parties," Trump said.
Tells Philippines, ASEAN that the US is staying engaged
Trump later joined Southeast Asian leaders for a special US-ASEAN summit and dinner. Addressing the room, he said Washington remained committed to the region's "success, sovereignty, and prosperity."
US President Donald Trump speaks during an official dinner at the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit in Manila on November 17, 2026.
Aaron Favila, pool via AFP
"We're with you always," Trump said.
He highlighted the US alliance with the Philippines and said defense cooperation had increased significantly.
"I don't think we've ever been closer than we are right now because of our personal relationship," Trump said of Marcos.

The Marcos administration has upgraded different areas of the country's ties with Washington while taking a more critical stance against China. It was a pivot from his predecessor Rodrigo Duterte's friendlier Beijing policies.

Turning to Marcos, Trump said: "We support our partners and our allies 100 percent. And when there's a problem, you'll call me. You'll call Marco (Rubio), you'll call others, and if they don't respond I'll take your call. I'll say, Marco, you're fired, you didn't respond fast enough."
Trump also urged ASEAN countries to expand cooperation on critical minerals, rare earths and magnets while promoting US partnerships in energy, technology and defense.
ASEAN and the United States finalized principles aimed at combating online scams during the special summit.
Marcos meeting ahead
Trump and Marcos are due to hold a formal bilateral meeting Wednesday before the US president leaves for Shenzhen.

Their talks are expected to cover the Philippine-US alliance, regional security and economic cooperation as both countries navigate tensions with China in the South China Sea. Malacañang had said Marcos would push for a reduction in the US's 12.5% tariff levied on exports.

Trump's arrival drew protests in Manila. Demonstrators criticized US foreign policy and called for the scrapping of Pax Silica, a US-led supply-chain initiative. — Camille Diola with reports from Agence France Presse

articles.title: Nvidia beats Q3 expectations in first report post-Jensen Huang
articles.summary: The AI chipmaker said it doubled its third-quarter revenue and confirmed that Jensen Huang would not be reinstated as CEO after a Chinese spy scandal.

image.caption: Huang, often seen wearing a black leather jacket, became a leading figure in the global AI boom [FILE: October 21, 2026]Image: Soeren Stache/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: US AI chip giant Nvidia doubled its third-quarter revenues to more than $115 billion (about €104.59 billion), the company said Tuesday.
Nvidia Chairman Harvey Jones also confirmed that the board of directors has no plans to bring back former CEO Jensen Huang.
Huang resigned on Thursday after a string of extramarital affairs came to light, including with a woman who is suspected of being a Chinese intelligence asset.
What did Nvidia say about the results and Huang?
In a statement on Tuesday, interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress said it is "business as usual" as the firm tries to move on from the Huang affair.
"Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people," Kress said in her first remarks since she was appointed last week.
She did not address Huang's resignation or the uncertainty surrounding his successor as Nvidia's CEO.
During an earnings call with Nvidia investors on Tuesday, Chairman Jones said the board had "unanimously accepted" Huang's resignation and "does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO."
Are AI companies becoming more powerful than governments?
Huang pitches return after 'outpouring' of support
The results, which exceeded expectations, were announced hours after Huang said he would be willing to return to the company if the board agreed.
After Huang's resignation, tech industry figures such as Elon Musk, as well as US President Donald Trump, called for Huang to be reinstated as part of a campaign called "Bring Jensen Back."

In a post on X — his first public statement since the scandal plunged the company and AI sector into crisis — Huang acknowledged that he had made "serious mistakes in his personal life" and had failed to "live up to the standards expected of everyone at" the company.
Huang also said he had received an "outpouring of calls from Nvidia's employees, investors, business partners, and customers" for him to return.
Who is Jensen Huang?
Huang, 63, co-founded Nvidia, which he led for more than three decades, turning it from a maker of graphics cards used in PC gaming into the dominant supplier of chips driving advanced AI models.
Under his leadership, Nvidia grew into one of the world's biggest — and most strategically important — companies.
Nvidia has been at the center of the AI boom that has pushed markets to record levels and spurred economic growth around the world.
Nvidia's chips are critical for training and operating advanced AI systems, making them crucial to governments, the military and the tech industry.

articles.title: Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years in US prison over Trump murder plot
articles.summary:
Asif Merchant, allegedly linked to Iran, found by court to have sought retribution over Qassem Suleimani death

A Pakistani man was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison on Tuesday for…

blocks.text: A Pakistani man was sentenced to more than 27 years in prison on Tuesday for plotting to assassinate Donald Trump in retaliation for the US killing of Revolutionary Guards commander Qassem Suleimani, the Department of Justice said.
Asif Merchant, who had alleged ties to Iran, sought to hire a hitman to assassinate a politician or a government official in the United States, a Brooklyn court found.
Suleimani, the head of Iran’s foreign military operations, was killed in a US drone strike in Baghdad in January 2020. Iranian officials have repeatedly vowed to avenge his killing.

Merchant had testified that he was forced into the plot to protect his family in the Iranian capital Tehran from the Guards, adding that he thought he would get caught before anyone was killed, multiple media outlets reported.

He said he was never ordered to kill a specific person but noted his Iranian contact had mentioned three people in connection with the plot – Trump, the former US president Joe Biden and former UN ambassador Nikki Haley.
But the United States attorney general, Todd Blanche, insisted on Tuesday that the plot was against Donald Trump.

“An Iranian agent who came to the United States to coordinate an assassination attempt against President Trump has been justly sentenced for his criminal conduct,” said Blanche after Merchant was sentenced to 330 months’ imprisonment.
“The Department of Justice will not tolerate foreign terrorist plots against our leaders and will not stop until those responsible are held accountable.”
US officials previously said Merchant had “close ties to Iran” and described his alleged plot as “straight out of the Iranian regime’s playbook”.
Merchant was arrested on 12 July 2024 as he planned to leave the country.

articles.title: Trade talks between top Canada, U.S. officials ramping up: sources
articles.summary: As talks with the Trump administration begin to ramp up once again, the prime minister's point man on Canada-U.S. trade has been meeting with his counterparts weekly in a more formal way, according…

image.caption: Chief trade negotiator Janice Charette and Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc arrive at a committee meeting in Ottawa on Tuesday. Sources tell CBC News that trade talks with the Trump administration are again ramping up. (Justin Tang/The Canadian Press)

blocks.text: Politics·New

As talks with the Trump administration begin to ramp up once again, the prime minister's point man on Canada-U.S. trade has been meeting with his counterparts weekly in a more formal way, according to three senior government officials.
No formal deal is on the table, work underway to reduce trade irritants

Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has not travelled to Washington, D.C., to meet with U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer or Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick since talks restarted earlier this month. But there have been phone and video calls happening on a regular basis, the sources say.
Canada's chief trade negotiator Janice Charette is usually also on these calls, according to the officials.
CBC News is not naming the sources because they were not authorized to speak publicly about the trade talks.
Canada urged to ramp up U.S outreach as Democrats target Trump's tariffs

The sources say while there is no formal deal on the table, both sides are working to remove trade irritants with the goal of eventually getting to one. Auto and steel tariffs remain key sticking points.

At this time, there are no plans for LeBlanc to travel to Washington for in-person talks, unlike over the summer, where both LeBlanc and Charette spent weeks working from the Canadian Embassy and met regularly at the U.S. trade representative's office.
But no deal was reached, and when talks fell apart the U.S. hit Canada with additional tariffs, prompting Canada to respond with countermeasures.
On Nov. 1, Prime Minister Mark Carney posted on social media saying teams from both countries would start working again on a trade deal.

"We all recognize that this period of trade uncertainty has created real challenges for Canadian businesses, workers, communities and of course the families of those affected," said LeBlanc at the international trade committee on Tuesday.

"We believe it is possible to make a deal that is, first and foremost, in the interest of Canada, but also in the interest of the United States, and ultimately also with our Mexican partners," he said in French.

items: Investigate Trump or work with him? Democrats debate best path forward

blocks.text: The Advisory Committee on Canada-U.S. Economic Relations — a group of experts appointed by the federal government — are set to meet virtually on Thursday, where they are expected to discuss the situation on the ground in Washington and how financial support for tariff-affected industries is being implemented.
It will be the first meeting since the midterm elections, which saw the Trump administration lose control of Congress.
Democratic lawmakers have pledged to repeal tariffs on Canadian goods, although Democrats lack the two-thirds majorities in both chambers required to shield legislation from a presidential veto.
LeBlanc has said Canada's approach to finding a deal will not change despite the new political makeup of the U.S. Congress.
Goal is lowest tariffs possible: Charette
On Tuesday, Charette was asked by Conservative Canada-U.S. trade critic Shuvaloy Majumdar about whether Canada is now looking for a deal without tariffs.

"Madame Charette, you had suggested long-term tariffs are something we might have to accept. Would you say that tariff-free trade is now off the table, that's a decision the government has taken? Is the government's goal still tariff-free trade?"

items: What the Republican midterm defeat means for Trump, the U.S. and Canada

blocks.text: Charette said the objective is to try to get as close as possible to tariff-free trade.
"I have suggested that we are trying to get to the lowest rate of tariffs on the narrowest basket of goods, with the most preferential access for Canadian businesses and Canadian workers," she said.
"But we do have another partner on the other side of the table and they have shown to date an unwillingness to enter into any arrangement in which there is full tariff-free trade."
ABOUT THE AUTHOR

Kate McKenna is a senior reporter with CBC’s parliamentary bureau in Ottawa, where she covers federal politics. She previously worked for CBC’s The Fifth Estate and in the Halifax, Montreal and Charlottetown newsrooms. Her investigative and breaking news coverage has won five RTDNA awards. She is the author of No Choice: The 30-Year Fight for Abortion on Prince Edward Island.

articles.title: Man accused of destroying US military plane at Shannon airport in Ireland
articles.summary:
Daithi O’Corrain, 48, is charged with destruction of US government property, after allegedly cutting hydraulic lines

An axe-wielding man breached a security perimeter and destroyed an…

blocks.text: An axe-wielding man breached a security perimeter and destroyed an American military plane while it was parked at an Irish airport, US prosecutors said.
Daithi O’Corrain, 48, is accused of cutting hydraulic lines, smashing cockpit gauges and pouring ball bearings into fuel tanks.

O’Corrain is charged with destruction of US government property in connection with the incident in April at Shannon airport in the west of Ireland, according to an indictment unsealed on Tuesday in Manhattan.
He is not in US custody and his arraignment on the charge has not been scheduled, the AP news agency reported. If convicted, he faces up to 10 years in prison.
The $60m (£45m) US Air National Guard C-130 Hercules, which had been en route to a military assignment in another country, was rendered inoperable and will not fly again, US prosecutors said.

blocks.caption: O’Corrain broke into the C-130 as it was parked on a taxiway by destroying a locking mechanism on the rear crew door, his indictment said. Photograph: US Department of Justice/PA

blocks.text: O’Corrain, described by supporters as an independent peace activist, was arrested immediately after the attack by Ireland’s police force, An Garda Síochána. He was charged with causing criminal damage and trespassing.
Manhattan US attorney Jamie McDonald said the indictment sends “a clear and powerful message that attacks on US military assets – and thus our national security – will not be tolerated.”
An online fundraiser organised by people describing themselves as O’Corrain’s friends said he disarmed the C-130 in protest against the US’s war with Iran and support for Israel’s war in Gaza.
O’Corrain plotted the attack on 11 April for months, US prosecutors said.

blocks.caption: Shattered C-130 cockpit instruments alongside cut wiring and hydraulic lines inside the plane. Photograph: US Department of Justice/PA

blocks.text: He searched online for information about the construction of the C-130, a quad-engine turboprop mainly used for transporting equipment and personnel, and looked up coordinates for sneaking on to the airport’s grounds, prosecutors allege.
O’Corrain subscribed to a phone app that provided live flight tracking and ordered capsules of gallium, a chemical that can corrode steel and break down aluminium, prosecutors added.
He is also accused of trying to contact someone who had been involved in a prior breach at Shannon airport, prosecutors said.
O’Corrain breached the airport’s perimeter at about 4.40 am and broke into the C-130 as it was parked on a taxiway by destroying a locking mechanism on the rear crew door, his indictment said.
The document added he used the crew’s hammocks to cover the plane’s windows but left the cockpit windshield exposed.

He then barricaded himself inside the aircraft, securing the doors with straps, brackets and screws, and put ball bearings mixed with epoxy in door tracks to prevent doors from being opened or closed, the indictment said.
James Barnacle, the head of the FBI’s New York office, said: “This was not an act of spontaneous vandalism.”
