articles.title: EU, ASEAN pursue deeper trade ties, but hurdles remain as businesses struggle with informal barriers
articles.summary: 2027 could be a landmark year for EU–Southeast Asia trade, with several deals nearing completion. But the harder task will be to ensure that businesses actually use them.

image.caption: The EU should focus on cutting customs delays, simplifying regulations, and helping smaller European businesses enter unfamiliar Southeast Asian markets, experts sayImage: Joseph Nair/NurPhoto/picture alliance

blocks.text: The European Union and the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) could be heading for a breakthrough year in 2027, when the two sides mark 50 years of diplomatic ties.

A long-awaited trade agreement with Indonesia is expected to take effect, while a deal with the Philippines is nearing completion and negotiations with Thailand and Malaysia are making progress. By the end of next year, the EU could have trade deals in place with six Southeast Asian states, up from just two today.
The anniversary could also revive the long-standing ambition of a broader trade agreement between the EU and ASEAN.
On November 17, the European Commission hosted a dialogue in Brussels to discuss trade relations with Southeast Asia, including progress on existing and pending free trade agreements (FTAs).
But attention is turning to what comes next. "Finalizing FTAs is only the beginning, not the end," Chris Humphrey, executive director of the EU-ASEAN Business Council, told DW.
FTAs can reduce tariffs and remove trade restrictions, but that is of little use if businesses don't know how to use them, he added.
"Unfortunately, in many cases, this is where there is a failure. Communication and training are key," Humphrey said.
Indonesia and EU finally seal landmark trade deal
The hard work begins after signing
For Brussels, the priority should now be to tackle the less conspicuous obstacles to trade, he stressed.
Cutting customs delays, simplifying regulations, and helping smaller European businesses enter unfamiliar Southeast Asian markets will determine whether an FTA succeeds.

"European companies with little or no experience in Southeast Asia would benefit from greater on-the-ground support, particularly practical, firsthand guidance on informal business practices and the unwritten local rules," Alfred Gerstl, an associate professor at Palacky University Olomouc in the Czech Republic, told DW.

One option is to expand the assistance offered by European chambers of commerce, trade delegations, and EU offices in Southeast Asia. This could range from helping firms find distributors to explaining local licensing requirements and how to qualify for preferential tariffs.

In Vietnam, for instance, sustained pressure from Brussels has helped improve market access for European pharmaceutical firms. In Indonesia, the EU has worked on trade facilitation while pressing Jakarta over import restrictions and halal certification requirements, said Camille Nessel, a researcher at the Université Libre de Bruxelles.
Regular consultations with businesses on both sides could also help Brussels spot problems before they become trade disputes.

Trade policy has also acquired a geopolitical purpose in Brussels. "If trade policy is expected to reduce strategic dependencies, we are asking it to deliver on objectives that remain insufficiently defined, let alone demonstrating how to achieve them," Nessel told DW.
Diversifying trade and reducing dependencies

The EU wants to reduce its dependence on a handful of suppliers for the minerals needed for batteries and other clean technologies, while Southeast Asian producers, particularly Indonesia, want foreign investors to help develop domestic processing industries rather than merely buy raw materials.
The EU and Indonesia have already clashed over Jakarta's restrictions on nickel exports.

European investment in processing facilities, agreements on environmental standards, and greater regulatory certainty would give both sides concrete gains, said Nessel. "The real value of an FTA is not just opening a market but giving the EU the leverage to keep it open," she added.

Pasha Hsieh, Lee Kong Chian Professor of Law and Jean Monnet Chair at Singapore Management University, said Brussels should prioritize ratifying its investment protection agreements with Singapore and Vietnam.

Signed in 2018 and 2019, respectively, the agreements still require ratification by all EU member states before entering into force. "These delays underline the need to follow through on negotiated commitments," Hsieh said.

The issue is particularly relevant as the EU looks to develop investment protocols in other Southeast Asian states where investors have sometimes faced uncertainty over legal protections. Indonesia, for instance, has terminated numerous bilateral investment treaties, including agreements with the Netherlands and Spain.
Towards an EU-ASEAN trade agreement?
A larger question is whether the EU should continue pursuing bilateral deals with Southeast Asian countries or revive its original ambition of a region-to-region agreement with ASEAN.

The EU and ASEAN launched negotiations for a region-wide FTA in 2007 but suspended them two years later amid disagreements over wide economic disparities among ASEAN members and political concerns. Technical discussions resumed in 2017, but little has come of them.
ASEAN already has regional agreements with China and several other economies. Beijing upgraded its free trade agreement with ASEAN in October 2025.
Trade Reset: How Europe is replacing China and the US

Region-to-region frameworks extend beyond trade. Humphrey, of the EU-ASEAN Business Council, called for negotiations to begin on a region-to-region Digital Trade Agreement and Investment Protection Agreement.

The EU-Singapore Digital Trade Agreement, which entered into force in February 2026, offers a possible model for wider cooperation, he noted, adding that common approaches to customs procedures, supply-chain standards, and green technologies could create greater alignment with ASEAN members that are not yet ready for full FTAs.

"European businesses have long complained of operating at a disadvantage due to the lack of a region-to-region deal. It is high time that both sides elevated their ambitions and embraced the idea of working towards such an agreement," Humphrey said.
The 2027 anniversary would be a convenient deadline for agreeing on what comes next, but Gerstl warned against mistaking another round of diplomatic ceremony for progress.

"There is a risk that attention will focus almost exclusively on the 2027 summit in Singapore and that the group photo will become the defining image of the event, only for momentum to fade in the years that follow," he added.

articles.summary: It marks the first sanctions since the UK announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.

blocks.text: The UK has sanctioned companies it said were involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank, in the first package of measures since the government announced a tougher approach to Israeli actions in the territory.
The government said the sanctions against eight construction and property development firms would disrupt their flows of finance and ability to support building in the West Bank.
Settlements are illegal under international law, and there has been a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers in recent months.
It comes two days before the deadline for bids for construction tenders in the E1 area east of Jerusalem.
The plans, which have been condemned internationally, would in effect divide the West Bank in two and isolate East Jerusalem.
UK Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband has said the E1 development would render a two-state solution "unviable" by "cutting through the heart of Palestine".
The sanctions also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement which the UK government says has organised and carried out blockades to prevent aid entering Gaza.

It comes after the UK expanded its human rights sanctions regime last month, enabling the government to sanction individuals and companies involved in violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world.
The government is also developing separate legislation to ban the import of settlement goods and the provision of advertising services for settlement properties in the UK.
Miliband said: "Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach.
"That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution.
"The status quo in the West Bank and Gaza is unacceptable.
"We are committed to working productively with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to advance lasting peace and security for Israelis and Palestinians alike."

articles.title: Palestinian woman, 72, shot dead by Israeli settlers in West Bank, health ministry says
articles.summary: Palestinians say there was an attack by settlers in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, while the Israeli military says the settlers fired after being attacked.

blocks.text: Image source, EPA
A funeral was held for Fadwa al-Fahidat in the village of al-Duyuk al-Tahta on Tuesday
ByYolande KnellMiddle East correspondentReporting fromJerusalem and David Gritten

A Palestinian woman in her 70s has been shot dead, and several other people wounded, in a village in the occupied West Bank where Israeli settlers recently moved in, the Palestinian health ministry says.

There are conflicting accounts of what happened. Local Palestinians said there was an attack by settlers in part of al-Duyuk al-Tahta, near Jericho, which is meant to be under the full control of the Palestinian Authority.
According to the Israeli army, there was a Palestinian car-ramming attack on an Israeli vehicle. It said rocks were then thrown at the Israelis, who opened fire in response.
There have been high tensions in the area since a group of settlers recently set up a new outpost.
They moved into eight houses in the village on 4 November after buying them, they have said, in a secretive operation. The properties are in an area where Israel retains full security control.
All settlements are illegal under international law.

blocks.caption: Image caption, Medics say Palestinians and Israelis were wounded in the incident on Monday evening

blocks.text: Image source, Reuters
Medics say Palestinians and Israelis were wounded in the incident on Monday evening
Palestinian reports said Fadwa al-Fahidat, who was 72, was shot outside her home on Monday evening and that, hearing the news, her son sped to the scene in his car.
He then collided with an empty Israeli vehicle parked outside his family home and settlers standing nearby were injured, they said. The settlers then began shooting, the reports said.

The statement from the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said that "terrorists accelerated their vehicle toward an Israeli vehicle and rammed it", and then "exited their vehicle with weapons and attacked and harmed the occupants of the Israeli vehicle".
Afterwards, it said, "rocks were hurled at the Israelis, who responded by firing in order to remove the threat." It did not mention the fatal shooting of a woman.
The IDF said that Israeli security forces were sent to the scene and were pursuing suspects.
Doctors at a hospital in Jericho said that al-Fahidat was shot in the head. Several other Palestinians and Israelis were injured, reports said.

The Israeli human rights group B'Tselem says there has been a prolonged campaign of settler attacks, intimidation and land seizures in al-Duyuk al-Tahta, with Israeli troops now stationed nearby to secure the new settlement.
Residents and activists say armed settlers walk and drive quad bikes around the neighbourhood as they threaten Palestinian residents.

blocks.caption: Image caption, A group of settlers set up a new outpost in al-Duyuk al-Tahta earlier this month (file photo)

blocks.text: A group of settlers set up a new outpost in al-Duyuk al-Tahta earlier this month (file photo)

In a separate incident on Monday evening, eight Palestinians were injured when they were hit by a vehicle driven by an Israeli settler on a main road in Tuqu, south of Bethlehem, according to Palestinian officials and the Palestinian Red Crescent.

The IDF said the incident was a traffic accident. But the Palestinian foreign ministry called it a "terrorist attack", saying the driver hit a group of Palestinians who had gathered near the scene of an earlier traffic accident.

Also on Monday, the Civil Administration - the body that implements Israeli government policy in the West Bank - announced the allocation of more than 28 sq km (6,945 acres) of land in the northern Jordan Valley to nine settlers for grazing, according to the Israeli anti-settlement watchdog Peace Now.

It said handing over vast tracts of land to settlers for grazing outposts constituted "direct support for the systematic expulsion of Palestinians from their lands and the rampant criminal violence in the West Bank".
The UK government said on Tuesday that it was imposing sanctions on eight companies building Israeli settlements in the West Bank.

It is the first sanctions package since Foreign Secretary David Miliband's pledge in September to respond to the accelerating rate of settlement expansion in the West Bank, which he said risked rendering a two-state solution unviable.

articles.title: Trump lands in Asia ahead of talks with Russian and Chinese presidents
articles.summary: The US president said he would be open to a one-on-one meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin "if it's available".

blocks.text: President Trump has arrived in the Philippines' capital on the first leg of a trip to Asia, which will end in a meeting in China with its President Xi Jinping and his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin.
A red carpet was rolled out for Trump as he walked off Air Force One in Manila. A band played one of his favourite songs, Y.M.C.A., before he was whisked away by helicopter to a hotel.

Trump's first meeting at the Asean Summit was with America's partners in the Quad - India's Narendra Modi, whom he described as a "very tough man", Japan's Sanae Takaichi, who "may be even tougher", and Australia's Anthony Albanese.
"Our countries are the four corners of the free, open, stable, prosperous Indo-Pacific," the US president said.
"We have outstanding relationships and co-ordinate closely... my phone is always open," Trump added.

Many countries in South East Asia have been hit hard by Donald Trump's tariffs and his war on Iran - but their exports to the US rose 30% last year thanks to the AI boom for which the region manufactures many of the components.
The US is hoping to draw more countries here into its "Pax Silica" tech and AI ecosystem, and away from China.
But China's huge influence in this region cannot easily be challenged, and certainly not in the few hours Trump is in the Philippines.
After an overnight stay in Manila, the US president will fly to Shenzhen in China to attend a summit of Asia Pacific leaders and have nuclear talks with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.
Asked if he would also be open to a one-on-one meeting with Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would".

articles.title: Trump meets regional allies in Manila ahead of China visit
articles.summary: It is Trump's first meeting of the Quad grouping and he says the leaders' discussions would include security and the development of artificial intelligence

blocks.text: QUAD LEADERS MEETING. US President Donald Trump, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi attend a Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue) summit, Paranaque City on November 17, 2026.
Carlos Barria/Reuters
It is Trump's first meeting of the Quad grouping and he says the leaders' discussions would include security and the development of artificial intelligence

MANILA, Philippines – US President Donald Trump met the leaders of regional allies India, Japan, and Australia in the Philippines on Tuesday, November 17, at the start of an Asian trip that also includes a much-anticipated trilateral meeting with his Chinese and Russian counterparts.

Trump arrived in the Philippine capital at the tail end of a Southeast Asian summit, and began his three-day regional visit with the first meeting in two years of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific democracies.

“Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” Trump said in remarks ahead of the meeting. “We have outstanding relationships and coordinate closely on matters of regional security, economic security and diplomacy.”

Trump’s three-day trip to Asia, which also includes the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, comes after his Republican Party’s defeat in midterm elections, plus spy allegations and new US curbs on China’s access to AI chips that could complicate a fragile trade-war truce.

blocks.caption: Spy scandal, US midterm defeat heat up Trump’s Asia visit

blocks.text: Demonstrators gathered in Manila for a fifth day of protests that have included the burning of Trump effigies, calls for an end to the Middle East war and the scrapping of the US-led Pax Silica supply chain initiative.

It was Trump’s first meeting of the Quad grouping — which his predecessor Joe Biden regarded as a signature foreign policy initiative — and he said the leaders’ discussions would include security and the development of artificial intelligence.

“We want to ensure that the future of this critical technology is dominated by nations that share our values and our common interests and make sure that it turns out to be as good as it can be,” Trump said, announcing the Quad would launch a new AI accelerator.
Trump arrived at the end of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations summit and after the Quad meeting will join a US-ASEAN “Special Summit” later on Tuesday.

It comes ahead of the APEC gathering hosted by Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has previously objected to the Quad as an effort to encircle Beijing. Quad members have said the grouping is not directed against any one country.

At the ASEAN summit on Monday, Chinese Premier Li Qiang hailed what he called the “truly extraordinary” economic achievements of China and ASEAN in the face of global trade restrictions, expressing Beijing’s commitment to free trade and the need to “stand united, ward off interference, and work together”.

China is ASEAN’s largest trading partner and a key source of investment, but the biggest economies of the 11-member bloc — which has a combined GDP of more than $3.9 trillion — want to deepen ties with the US despite protracted trade and diplomatic uncertainty under the Trump administration.
Former US Deputy Secretary of State Kurt Campbell credited Washington’s top diplomat, Marco Rubio, with the timing and reconvening of the Quad, which he said had lost ambition under Trump.

“Part of what he (Rubio) is thinking is that this is probably the best possible signal if you’re going to go into a trilateral meeting,” said Campbell, co-founder of The Asia Group, referring to Thursday’s US-China-Russia talks.
“The linchpin of everything that we do in Asia is the US-Japan relationship, and a perception that this is not at the top of the president’s mind would concern me.”

White House spokesperson Olivia Wales on Friday said that under Trump’s leadership, the Quad had demonstrated it is “a partnership of action, tackling the region’s toughest challenges and driving opportunities to ensure a free and open Indo-Pacific.”

A Japanese foreign ministry official said it was expected that Quad leaders would try to show unity, with maritime security, export restrictions, critical-minerals supply-chain diversification and AI among potential discussion points.
ASEAN’s leaders held meetings on Tuesday involving counterparts from Japan, South Korea, China, and India.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi pledged to work with ASEAN to boost regional economic and energy resilience, to address export restrictions and vulnerabilities from rapid AI development, and to strengthen supply chains, including on critical minerals.
“While the international order is experiencing a period of great instability, Japan will play an ever more proactive role,” Takaichi said.

blocks.caption: Japan proposes creation of ‘Asian’ IEA

blocks.text: Trump was due to sign a joint statement with Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul on Tuesday on an agreement on reciprocal trade. Thai media have reported the two would hold talks and the statement would be about progress on negotiations.
The US is Thailand’s largest export market, accounting for 24% of its total shipments this year. The US designated Thailand as a major non-NATO ally in 2003.
Trump will meet Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr on Wednesday, before heading to Shenzhen. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Guinea jails 200 in wildcat gold mining crackdown
articles.summary: A Conakry court has jailed 22 former local officials from the gold-rich northeastern Siguiri region, as well as 200 people accused of illegal mining. It's part of a wider crackdown that sent…

image.caption: More than 1,000 alleged artisanal gold miners are being tried in Conakry courts in various sessions, such as this one on November 11Image: Adrien Marotte/AFP

blocks.text: Guinea on Tuesday jailed 22 former regional administrators and 202 others accused of illegal gold mining in the northeastern Siguiri region near the border to Mali.
This comes as part of a wider crackdown on wildcat mining that has led to violent clashes and forced thousands of people to flee into Mali.
According to the UN Environment Program, unauthorized gold mining is a source of income for more than 300,000 people in Guinea. The country's rich gold mines pull in workers from across West Africa.

blocks.caption: Conakry's economic and financial crimes court issued the sentences on TuesdayImage: Adrien Marotte/AFP

blocks.text: What happened in the gold mining trial in Conakry?

Conakry's Court for the Repression of Economic and Financial Offenses sentenced 22 former officials from Siguiri to two years each in prison for complicity in environmental degradation, destruction and water pollution. They were each fined 10 million Guinean francs (around €1,025 or $1,125).
The court also sentenced 202 alleged illegal miners — several of them foreign nationals — to three-year prison sentences. They faced the same charges plus an additional count of mining illegally.
They were ordered to pay a combined fine of 10 billion Guinean francs.
Beyond that, the foreign nationals were banned from Guinean territory for a period of 10 years.

blocks.caption: Many miners fled this month's crackdown into neighboring Mali, where they crowded to wait for transportation home to Burkina FasoImage: AFP

blocks.text: Why is Guinea cracking down on illegal mining?
Guinea's government announced a bid to stamp out illegal gold mining earlier this month, saying it wanted to prevent damages to farmland and rivers and other environmental destruction.
These efforts turned violent last week as protesters and security forces clashed in the northeast, with 10 people killed and 13 injured.
More than 1,200 artisanal miners were arrested in Siguiri in November.
Many more fled across the border to nearby Mali, often then having to await transportation to their homes in Burkina Faso.

blocks.caption: Malian authorities say that a total of around 160,000 people have flooded into the country after being driven out of Guinea's gold-rich border regionsImage: AFP

articles.title: US flexes climate action muscle at COP31 despite Trump no-show
articles.summary: The US government is snubbing UN climate talks in Turkey. That's prompted a delegation of American lawmakers, mayors and governors to make the trip instead, aiming to show climate action in the US is…

image.caption: Minnesota Governor Tim Walz, the 2024 Democratic vice presidential candidate, traveled to Antalya with the delegationImage: Khalil Hamra/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: The United States, isn't at the table at the UN climate conference in the Turkish coastal city of Antalya. It's the second consecutive year that President Donald Trump, who has repeatedly said he believes climate change is a hoax, has not sent a federal delegation to the annual summit.
But that doesn't mean the US is totally absent. Far from it, since more than 120 state and local leaders from across the country are attending as part of the "America Is All In" coalition.
"We understand the importance of showing up. And if others refuse to do so, we will," said Chris Wheat, executive director of the coalition.
It's crucial, he added, to show the world that "millions of Americans are continuing to press forward on climate action" — even if the message from Washington, D.C., is a different one.

blocks.caption: The 'America is All In' pavilion has been the base for the US presence at this year's COPImage: Kaan Soyturk/REUTERS

blocks.text: Historically, the US has released more emissions than any other country, and it is currently the world's second-biggest emitter of planet-warming greenhouse gases after China. Since taking office in January 2025, Trump has actively promoted the use of oil, coal and gas, the fossil fuels that are heating the planet and contributing to an increase in extreme weather events.
The president has also cut funds for clean energy projects and rolled back some of the climate policies of his predecessors, such as rules limiting power plant emissions.
Momentum beyond White House

The unofficial US delegation of mainly Democrat lawmakers, mayors, governors and ex-officials — including former Secretary of State John Kerry, former Vice President Al Gore and California Governor Gavin Newsom — are not taking part in the climate negotiations. But they have been holding discussions at events on the conference sidelines.
They are keen to send a message to the international community that, despite their government's absence, efforts to transition to clean energy are gathering pace at the state level.
Does Gen Z care about the UN's big climate summit?
To play this audio please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 audio

Mike Williams, a senior fellow at the Center for American Progress, an independent liberal public policy research institute based in Washington D.C., said the presence of US lawmakers in Antalya sends an important signal that "there's quite a lot of us in the US that are still deeply invested in this. It's not just the person sitting in the White House."

Nearly half of US states, representing about 60% of the US economy, are committed to reducing emissions in line with the Paris Agreement — the 2015 global pact to limit global warming. Many have implemented initiatives such as tax incentives for renewables and other policies designed to curb emissions.

A report by America Is All In and the University of Maryland's Center for Global Sustainability found that current state policies, combined with market trends and falling technology costs, could slash US carbon emissions by up to 46% below 2005 levels by 2035.
States tout climate action

"Even if we find a hostile federal government, they're not going to be able to stop the momentum," Minnesota Governor Tim Walz told a crowd at the summit in Turkey, adding that his state was on track to have a "100% carbon free" grid by 2037, earlier than their target of 2040.

Walz said the state was also producing sustainable aviation fuel to reduce flight emissions, manufacturing green steel and increasing the share of electric vehicles. "It's all moving forward," he said. "So this false choice that we need to choose the economy over clean energy — that has been totally rejected."

blocks.caption: New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham said her state had drastically curbed methane emissionsImage: Rich Crowder/GE Vernova/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: New Mexico Governor Michelle Lujan Grisham said her state — the second-largest oil and gas producer in the US — had significantly cut emissions from the potent greenhouse gas methane through stricter regulations. She also touted measures such as shutting down coal power plants and expanding wind and solar energy.

"The largest wind farm in North America is in New Mexico," she said. "We're going to show the federal government, I am undaunted by their lack of responsibility and effort in cleaning up fossil fuels."
What's next for US climate policy after midterms?

The climate conference comes shortly after the US midterm elections, in which Trump's Republicans suffered a significant defeat. Democrats in Antalya have been keen to reassure the international community that the US would return to the COP table in the event of a change of government in two years.

Jorge Gastelumendi, senior director of the Atlantic Council's Climate Resilience Center, noted that US credibility around climate change and foreign policy in general had been "badly damaged" under Trump. "And so it's going to be a matter of how that could be built back up," he said.

Meanwhile, Governor Newsom of California, a state of around 40 million people that plans to get 100% of its energy from renewables by 2045, said the US administration's climate withdrawal was also hurting the country's competitiveness.
COP31: Can electrification replace fossil fuels?

"We need to reengage in these international agreements, and we need to recognize that China is outpacing us in many critical areas," such as solar power and electric cars, he told reporters in Antalya. "There is no substitute for national leadership."
Williams from the Center for American Progress said he wouldn't hold it against any countries wary about the US returning to the climate negotiations after two exits under Trump.

"Nobody should be under any perception that the US would be welcomed back with open arms," he said. "I think there needs to be an effort to show a willingness to collaborate […] That's another reason why it's important we're here now to show that there is this very large undercurrent of support within the US in spite of what's happening."
Additional reporting from Tim Schauenberg in Antalya.

articles.title: Students' List candidates take seats as Serbian parliament opens
articles.summary: Serbia's Student List's candidates have taken their oaths in the inaugural parliament session. As the new majority, they have 90 days to form a government.

image.caption: The Students' List has pledged many reforms in domestic politicsImage: Darko Vojinovic/AP Photo/picture alliance

blocks.text: Representatives of Serbia's student-led movement were sworn in as lawmakers on Tuesday, just over four weeks after they ended Serbia's strongman leader Aleksandar Vucic's 14 years of rule.
The Students' List candidates officially took their seats in the inaugural parliamentary session as the first step for the youth-backed party toward forming Serbia's new government.
The movement holds 140 seats in the 250-member parliament while Vucic's right-wing Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) holds 103. The remaining seats belong to ethnic minority parties.
Serbia's student-led movement ends Vucic era

Hundreds gathered outside the parliament building in the capital Belgrade, to show their support for the student-backed lawmakers, most of whom are teachers, professors and other professionals with little or no political experience.
Meanwhile, SNS candidates were met with a negative reaction from the crowd. A woman in the crowd poured yogurt over an SNS member's head as she climbed the steps to the parliament entrance.

According to Serbian media, the newly elected lawmakers have been preparing for their first session for days. They will face veteran opposition politicians, including Aleksandar Vucic, who became the opposition leader after his defeat.
90 days to form a government
The Students' List will have 90 days to name a prime minister, present their programme and form a government, once the parliament is formed.
Lessons from Serbia: how students defeated an authoritarian leader

The movement unites left- and right-wingers, pro-European and pro-Russian forces. It is focused on making changes in domestic politics and wants to advance European Union accession talks by implementing real reforms. The List opposes sanctions on Russia and the recognition of Kosovo — positions that almost the entire population of Serbia agrees with.
They pledged to improve healthcare, boost education and double the defense budget, along with many other reforms.
The election of a new parliamentary speaker will also lead to the appointment of a new acting president. The speaker has held the role since Vucic resigned in September to run for prime minister.
A snap presidential election must be called by November 27 and held by December 27.
Both parties are expected to put forward presidential candidates, but Vucic cannot seek another term because the constitution limits presidents to two terms in office.
Ready to break free: How Serbia's media are changing

articles.title: Caloocan DPWH deals with Malapitan kin raise conflict-of-interest questions
articles.summary: Mayor Along Malapitan is the son-in-law of a government contractor who had won DPWH projects in Caloocan City, mostly in the 1st District where his father, Oscar, is congressman

blocks.text: There are many government contractors in Caloocan City, but one, in particular, got the attention of locals because of its links to the city’s dominant political dynasty.
The contractor drew little attention outside Caloocan, even when it appeared on a list of alleged Malacañang-dictated budget insertions cited by fugitive resigned lawmaker Zaldy Co in November 2025.

After months in hiding following his implication in the flood control scandal, Co broke his silence with a series of Facebook videos. He tagged President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. and then-speaker Martin Romualdez as the alleged masterminds of P100 billion in insertions in the 2025 budget.

Co released a 20-page list of insertions that Marcos allegedly requested, through Palace officials, at the bicameral conference committee level. He claimed he never received a single centavo from government coffers. Malacañang and Romualdez denied the allegations and challenged him to submit them formally under oath.
Two projects on Co’s list, worth a total of P188 million, named Ave-Mira Construction and Trading as contractor.

Days after Co’s bombshell, concerned citizen Christopher Orongan, a former soldier, asked on Facebook: “Marami yatang projects sa Caloocan itong Ave-Mira Construction and Trading. Sino kaya ang may-ari nito? Kilala ba?”
(Ave-Mira Construction and Trading seems to have many projects in Caloocan. I wonder who its owner is? Are they known?)

Five days later, Orongan asked a more pointed question: “Sino si Avelino Narciso? Related ba sa asawa ng kasalukuyang Mayor ng Caloocan City (Who is Avelino Narciso? Is he related to the wife of the incumbent Caloocan City mayor)?”

Even after Orongan answered his own question, the posts gained little traction. Interest was localized, limited to Caloocan netizens or those aware of city politics. Public attention was focused on the top 15 flood control contractors Marcos had named months earlier, the resulting congressional inquiries, and the fugitive Co.
The government investigation into flood control corruption was already in full swing, after Marcos formed the Independent Commission for Infrastructure (ICI) in September 2025.
Ave-Mira was established in Orani, Bataan, and is named after owner Avelino Narciso and his wife, Edelmira. Their daughter, Aubrey, is the wife of Caloocan City Mayor Dale Gonzalo “Along” Malapitan.
The company’s General Information Sheet filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission in July 2025 lists the following:

items: Narciso as the corporate secretary with a 33% share
Son-in-law Rome Sicat as chairman with 33.5%
Sicat’s wife, Abba Narciso Sicat, as treasurer with 33.5%

blocks.text: Rome and Abba both served on the Orani Municipal Council. Rome was town councilor from 2010 to 2019, while Abba was first elected in 2019 and is on her third term.

Ave-Mira began getting Department of Public Works and Highways contracts in 2019, starting with a project in Orani. That year, it secured eight DPWH contracts: seven in Bataan and one in Caloocan. Its other contracts are as follows:

items: Bataan, 2019 to 2025: 49 contracts worth P727,956,762.16. 14 of them were in Orani.

Bulacan, 2021 to 2024: P51,463,463 worth of road, building and flood control contracts under the Bulacan 1st District Engineering Office. Senator Panfilo Lacson highlighted that office in his August 2025 privilege speech on flood control corruption.
Quezon City: the company also secured government contracts here.

blocks.text: The Malapitans’ rise to the dominant political dynasty in Caloocan City started with their patriarch, Oscar, who served as Caloocan councilor from 1992 to 1998, vice mayor from 1998 to 2001, and 1st District congressman from 2004 to 2013. He was mayor from 2013 to 2022, and has been congressman again since 2022.

Along was 1st District councilor when he married Aubrey Narciso in 2013. That year, he sought his father’s congressional seat but lost to then-outgoing mayor Recom Echiverri. He ran again in 2016 and won.
He was reelected in 2019, and by the end of his second term in 2022, his father was a term-limited mayor. The two won each other’s posts in the 2022 elections and were both reelected in 2025.
Along’s brother, Enteng, entered politics in 2019 as a 1st District councilor. He won a third term in 2025 and will serve until 2028.

Narciso was among Along’s donors in the last two elections. He donated P3 million to his son-in-law’s 2022 election campaign, and the same amount to his 2025 election campaign, according to Along’s Statements of Contributions and Expenditures (SOCEs) obtained by Rappler from the Commission on Elections (Comelec).

From 2019 to 2025, while Along and Oscar were either congressman or city mayor, Ave-Mira got 39 DPWH projects in Caloocan City worth P731,368,859.87. Two were joint ventures with Orani Construction and Supply Corporation.
In early November 2024, Congressman Malapitan and Mayor Along led the blessing and turnover of covered courts in Barangays 174 and 176, both in the 1st District.

A post on the congressman’s official Facebook page was accompanied by his photos with Along. It said in part, “Mula sa pondong inilaan ni Congressman Oca Malapitan sa mga proyektong ito, binuksan ito sa publiko partikular sa mga residente upang kanilang magamit at pagdausan ng iba’t ibang aktibidad.”
(From the funds allocated by Congressman Oca Malapitan for these projects, these were opened to the public particularly for the residents’ use and for their activities.)
The post added that the congressman will continue supporting the Caloocan government’s goals of building more infrastructure for the people’s welfare and community development.
The Barangay 176 covered court cost P4,876,621.09, and the Barangay 174 covered court, P6,805,023.78. Ave-Mira was the contractor for both courts.
Based on contracts on the DPWH website, covered courts in Metro Manila typically cost at least P4.8 million in 2024, but could cost double that, or more, depending on size and features.
Rappler asked the DPWH Metro Manila 3rd District Engineering Office, which implemented the projects, how Ave-Mira’s Caloocan contracts were procured.

In a letter, it replied: “Based on official records, the projects were procured and implemented in accordance with applicable procurement laws, rules, regulations, and DPWH procedures. Any variation orders, extensions, additional works, or other modifications, if applicable, were likewise processed in accordance with existing rules.”

District Engineer Maria Cristina Tacardon added: “No formal complaint from the concerned end-users regarding project implementation has been received or recorded by this Office. However, this does not cover concerns raised through other channels.”
On possible communications, endorsements, recommendations or interventions in choosing Ave-Mira, she said her office “can only confirm matters supported by official records.”

We reached out to Mayor Along’s office from September 21 to November 6 through his and city hall’s official emails, asking about possible conflicts of interest. A physical letter sent to city hall on November 4 was acknowledged and received the same day.
We also contacted Ave-Mira through the email addresses in their GIS on September 21, and followed up by text and Viber until November 7.
We will update this story once they respond.

The Philippine Constitution and various laws prohibit conflicts of interest. Politicians are barred from holding paid occupations other than their elective posts, and from having direct or indirect financial interests in government contracts.

The Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, Section 4(c) states: Public officials and employees “shall not dispense or extend undue favors on account of their office to their relatives whether by consanguinity or affinity.”

The Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, Section 4(a) also states: It is illegal for any person having a familial relationship with any public official to take advantage of it by directly or indirectly requesting or receiving an advantage from “any other person having some business, transaction, application, request or contract with the government, in which such public official has to intervene.”

Meanwhile, Section 89(a) of the Local Government Code prohibits local public officials and employees from directly or indirectly engaging in a business transaction in a local government unit where they serve.
Congress has proposed measures to address the problem of conflict of interest.

items: Senate Bill No. 1962 (Government Contracting and Procurement Act), approved on final reading in September: It would ban relatives of public officials within the fourth degree of consanguinity and affinity from all government contracts. The House version is pending.

House Bill No. 9142 (Electoral Conflict of Interest Prevention Act): It would require candidates to submit a sworn declaration that they and their immediate family have had no interest in government contracts in the five years before filing their certificate of candidacy.

House Bill No. 9906 (New Party-list System Act): It would bar political dynasty members, incumbent elective officials, recent electoral candidates, and persons with direct financial interests in government contracts from being party-list nominees.

blocks.text: The push for more laws shows how difficult it is to address conflict of interest. This is magnified by the infrastructure corruption scandal and the proliferation of “politicontractors.”

Asked about Ave-Mira’s Caloocan contracts, People’s Budget Coalition national coordinator Mary Abigail Modales told Rappler: “Is there potential conflict of interest? Yes, there is potential conflict of interest. But before we reach a conclusion, we have to be careful because we’re accusing someone of conflict of interest.”

Modales said that to determine conflict of interest, these issues must first be addressed: beneficial ownership of the company, degree of relationship, receipt of undue benefit, and if the biddings were rigged or influenced by a public official to favor a contractor.
GoodGovPH chairperson Bryan Ezra Gonzales said ordinary citizens should know how to spot red flags in government projects and what to do about them.

He cited transparency watchdogs and government feedback mechanisms — Bisto Proyekto, Sumbong sa Pangulo, the Department of Budget and Management’s Project Digital Information for Monitoring and Evaluation (DIME), and the DPWH which, he said, has been “pro-active” on complaints under Vince Dizon.
He also acknowledged that many people are wary of becoming a whistleblower, underscoring the need for better government protection for them.

With the country nearing another election year, Gonzales offered a reminder: “One way wherein the public can collectively hold someone to account, someone in elective office, is to vote them out.” – Rappler.com

Eunicito Barreno is a 2026 Aries Rufo Fellow. He is a senior journalism student at the University of the Philippines Diliman, where he is also a news staffer at the Philippine Collegian, the university’s official student publication.

articles.title: Gunmen kill Costa Rican journalist who reported on drugs trade
articles.summary: Rodríguez had denounced alleged links between criminal organisations and powerful figures in Costa Rica.

blocks.text: A Costa Rican journalist who denounced alleged links between politicians and drug traffickers in the Central American country has been shot dead.
Police said gunmen on a motorbike ambushed Camilo Rodríguez, 50, as he was travelling in his car north of the capital, San José, on Monday afternoon.
The independent reporter earlier said he had been receiving death threats from drug trafficking gangs.

Local media reported that it was the first murder of a journalist in more than two decades in Costa Rica. It comes at a time when transnational crime gangs are increasing their presence in the country, driving up its formerly low homicide rate.

The president of the Costa Rican Journalists' Association, Yanancy Noguera, said that "all evidence so far points to the silencing of a dissenting voice in Costa Rica - a person who published information about organised crime in the country".
Rodríguez had been working as a journalist for several decades, both in radio and in print.

Most recently, he had been uploading videos to social media in which he named public figures such as judges, business people and politicians, which he alleged were corrupt or had ties to known drug traffickers.
In one of his videos, he alleged that the home of Costa Rica's President, Laura Fernández, had been constructed by a company that he said had links to a criminal gang.
Fernández, who categorically denied any wrongdoing, took the journalist to court, accusing him of defamation.
Reacting to his murder in a video message, the president strongly condemned the attack, calling it "a stain on freedom of expression".
She added that she had instructed police to do their utmost to "punish Camilo's murderers".
Rodríguez had also tried to stand for political office, seeking to run as the presidential candidate for the Costa Rican Renovation Party in 2021.
However, his candidacy was rejected by the electoral authorities after the party failed to meet the necessary criteria required to file candidates.

Costa Rica's Attorney General, Carlo Díaz, said that "silencing someone who reports on drug trafficking or corruption, in this case a communicator, is a signal we cannot tolerate in a democratic society".

articles.title: Klopp and Wirtz offer glimpse of bright German future
articles.summary: Germany's fall from grace in recent years has seen the team drift away from the fans. But Monday's drubbing of the Netherlands and the impact of Jürgen Klopp, Florian Wirtz and emerging youngsters…

image.caption: Jürgen Klopp has got the best out of Florian Wirtz in a Germany shirtImage: Tom Weller/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: "Extraordinary," "Insane," "Magnificent," "A special group." Even by Jürgen Klopp's effusive standards, Germany's 5-0 win over rivals the Netherlands on Monday was clearly pleasing.
Despite a patchy start to his reign, Klopp's relentless positivity towards a group of Germany players not viewed in the most flattering light outside the squad has been rewarded.

"Everyone will go home with a smile on their face, and for at least the next three or four months, no one will be questioning the German national team," Klopp told German public broadcaster ARD, referencing that Germany will not play again until the end of March 2027.
"Instead, they'll be thinking: 'This could really turn into something. We have wonderful footballers, great characters," Klopp said, and added: "The lads are even surprising themselves."

The former Liverpool and Borussia Dortmund coach took the job in July after Julian Nagelsmann paid the price for another German early World Cup exit, this time to Paraguay in the last 32. Klopp always preached patience, particularly after his first two matches yielded a fortunate 1-1 draw with the Netherlands and a 1-0 home loss to Greece.
Klopp hallmarks starting to emerge

It paid off on Monday as Germany performed with the hallmarks of Klopp's great club sides — fierce pressing, intensity, pace and a measure of joy. Perhaps it is in Florian Wirtz that Klopp's impact is more notable.

The 23-year-old has struggled to make a significant impact at Liverpool since moving to the Premier League from Bayer Leverkusen at the beginning of last season. But he has four goals in his last four games for Germany and is demonstrating the ability that earned him a €125 million ($137.5 million) move to England.
"I only knew him from television. I was shocked when I saw him on the pitch for the first time. An extraordinary footballer," Klopp said after the Netherlands match.
"We've also found the right position for Flo. It helps that he's so vocal. He's the first pressing player, he can press two players without getting tired."

blocks.caption: Florian Wirtz has scored more goals for Germany than for Liverpool this seasonImage: DeFodi Images/IMAGO

blocks.text: That quality was evident in Wirtz's first goal on Monday, when he won back possession on the edge of the Dutch box before combining some dazzling footwork with a brilliant, curled finish.
Scherhant, Gruda and Wirtz make their cases

But Wirtz wasn't the only attacking bright spot for Germany. Rookie wingers Derry Scherhant and Brajan Gruda both scored and were a huge threat throughout. Klopp gave debuts to both earlier this year as he sought to spread opportunities. The pair have offered Germany a pace they often lacked under Naglesmann and his predecessor Hansi Flick.
"They can both play, my goodness," said Klopp.

Scherhant, who opened the scoring with another stunning strike, spent many days of his boyhood on the terraces of the Olympiastadion in Berlin, where Monday's game was played. Unlike many pros, he bounced about Berlin's lower league clubs as a youth before Hertha Berlin signed him up. He then moved to Freiburg in 2025 and is rapidly emerging as a player who can implement Klopp's style and reflect the coach's attitude.

"A few years ago, people told me I wouldn't make it as a pro. Then I became a pro. And even then, some people still said it wasn't enough—that the Regionalliga (Germany's fourth tier) was the best I could hope for,” Scherhant said.
"It's just unbelievable that I get to stand here now with the satisfaction of having proven those people wrong."

blocks.caption: Jürgen Klopp's faith in Derry Scherhant is starting to pay offImage: Marc Schueler/Sportpics/picture alliance

blocks.text: Proving people wrong is also a major part of Klopp's remit. After failing to get beyond the quarterfinal of a major tournament since 2016, the German public's interest in and enthusiasm for its men's national team had waned. Klopp's mission he said, was to "to prove to Germany and the world that we can play soccer."
Germany need to change perceptions

While that was achieved on Monday, the loss (and subsequent 0-0 draw) against Greece in the Nations League game were evidence that it won't all be plain sailing. Indeed, Germany have had plenty of false dawns of late, as captain Joshua Kimmich alluded to.

"We've been through a tough time," he said. "A clear victory doesn't make all that go away," he added before saying that the task was to "turn potential into quality and a team that's all about 'what ifs' into a team that's all about 'reality.' That's the art of it."
Klopp too, for all his hype, was keen not to get too far ahead of himself.
"We want to gradually solidify it. We're not done yet. We still have a few areas to work on. But I'm looking forward to our future — it's crazy what's still to come," he said.

In Nations League terms, that will be a matchup with world champions Spain, or Portugal or Belgium before qualifying for Euro 2028 begins. For now though, Klopp and his players can enjoy some time with those smiles on their faces.

articles.title: Democrats’ Peltola ahead as counting nears end in Alaska Senate race – US politics live
articles.summary: Challenger nears 50% of the ballot to secure victory in final midterms contest

blocks.text: Key events

items: 10m agoAlaska midterm race could be called on Wednesday as Peltola remains ahead of Republican incumbent

blocks.text: Alaska midterm race could be called on Wednesday as Peltola remains ahead of Republican incumbent
Hello and welcome to the US politics live blog.
The final Senate race of this year’s midterm elections could be resolved tomorrow if Alaska election officials run the state’s ranked choice voting system to determine the result.

With 98% of ballots counted, Democratic challenger Mary Peltola is out in front with 49.98% of the vote. By contrast, incumbent Republican senator Dan S Sullivan has a 45.93% share, according to the latest Associated Press figures.

In terms of actual voting numbers, Peltola is ahead by just over 11,000, with 141,637 compared to Sullivan’s 130,162. All eyes will be on Peltola to see if she can keep the pace to achieve 50% of the ballot, two weeks on from the election.
If not, then voters’ second choice votes will be counted. The outcome will determine the final balance of power in the chamber for the next two years, with Democrats already holding a 55-44 majority.

It comes in a turbulent Alaska race, which has seen president Trump demand that Peltola be removed from the ballot and prosecuted. Piling on, Alaska’s Republican governor has since ordered an investigation into Peltola’s campaign.

A New York Times investigation reported that operatives working with Peltola’s campaign helped recruit another Dan Sullivan – Dan J Sullivan – a retired teacher from Petersburg, to split the incumbent’s vote. Peltola and her campaign have denied this.

The ‘other’ Sullivan, who stood as an independent candidate, has only received 4,684 votes – a 1.65% share – and is looking unlikely to be the cause of the Republican senator’s failure should he not retain his seat.

Elsewhere, president Trump has arrived in Manila, the capital of the Philippines, for the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit, where he is due to meet south east Asian leaders and take part in the first leaders’ meeting of the Quad partnership – consisting of the US, Japan, India and Australia – since he returned to the White House in January 2025.
You can follow that here:
In other developments:

items: Donald Trump defended his commerce secretary Howard Lutnick after he came under fire for allegedly slow-walking export restrictions on Nvidia chips to China. This comes after treasury secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC last week that he has been pushing “for months” to add Megaspeed, the data center company led by an alleged Chinese spy who was reportedly in a relationship with ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, to the US trade blacklist.

Trump blasted the new leadership of CBS News’ 60 Minutes, which was overhauled under the network’s conservative editor-in-chief Bari Weiss. In a social media post, the president was particularly critical of a report on the more than 800 American service members wounded and 23 killed in the war in Iran that 60 Minutes aired on Sunday.

⁠Trump also said that he ⁠would ​“not ‌mind” ‌seeing Jensen ‌Huang reinstated as the chief executive ‌officer of ​Nvidia. The president says the ex-CEO has learned a lesson, and denied that national security has been put at risk.

The president also continued to shift responsibility to the Biden administration for the nationwide ground stop over the weekend. Trump said that he needed more funding to overhaul the outdated telecommunication system responsible for the disruptions.

The Trump administration has warned Elizabeth Warren, the senior Democratic senator expected to chair the powerful Senate banking committee, that she could face “significant legal consequences” if she fails to preserve records related to investigations into Donald Trump. The warning mirrors other letters justice department officials have sent to Democratic lawmakers who have indicated they will investigate the Trump administration when the party becomes the majority in Congress next year.

A federal appeals court heard arguments in Donald Trump’s hush money case, as the president tries to see the case shifted to federal court where he could have it dismissed on grounds of immunity. The hearing concerned a May 2024 ruling that found Trump guilty on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to obscure a $130,000 payment to adult film star Stormy Daniels.

articles.title: ASEAN adopts first regional space cooperation pact
articles.summary: Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have adopted the bloc"s first declaration dedicated exclusively to space cooperation, marking a milestone in regional efforts to advance…

blocks.text: Published November 17, 2026 7:49pm

Leaders of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) have adopted the bloc’s first declaration dedicated exclusively to space cooperation, marking a milestone in regional efforts to advance space science and technology.

The ASEAN Leaders’ Declaration on the Advancement of Space Science, Technology and Innovation Cooperation was spearheaded by the Philippines through the Philippine Space Agency (PhilSA) during the 49th ASEAN Summit.

PhilSA said the declaration reflects the collective commitment of ASEAN member states to strengthen regional collaboration in space science and technology and expand the use of space applications across the region.

“More than a formal statement, this Declaration reflects a shared regional vision to strengthen collaboration in space science, technology, and innovation,” PhilSA Director General Gay Jane Perez said in a press release on Tuesday.

“Through this, we hope to further advance ASEAN’s collective capacity to harness space technologies in support of disaster resilience, environmental sustainability, economic growth, and inclusive development across our region,” she added.
The declaration identifies three key pillars of cooperation: space security and safety, space economy, and space workforce development.
It also aims to promote joint research, expand capacity-building programs, and encourage the sharing of space infrastructure and data among member states.

The declaration recognizes the differences in development levels, technological readiness, institutional capacities, and space capabilities among ASEAN members, while committing to ensure that no member state is left behind through equitable cooperation, capacity building, knowledge sharing, and mutual support.

Signed on Nov. 15, 2026, the declaration was endorsed by all 11 ASEAN member states: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Timor-Leste, and Vietnam.— MCG, GMA News

President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr. said the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) and China are now finalizing the "definition of terms" in the South China Sea Code of Conduct (COC), as the negotiations failed to be completed under the Philippines' chairmanship.

During a press briefing following the culmination of the ASEAN Summit, Marcos said there are terms that need to be understood and norms accepted by the parties, noting that the negotiations has reached 85%-90% under the Philippines' ASEAN chairmanship.

The COC was earlier described as "80% complete," with Foreign Secretary Ma. Theresa Lazaro saying it is now expected to be finished during Singapore's chairmanship of ASEAN next year. The Philippines maintains that non-completion is not a failure, citing time constraints. — BM, GMA News

articles.title: What will Gamaliel Cordoba, Marcos’ newest SC pick, bring to Padre Faura?
articles.summary: Cordoba was the NTC commissioner when the Duterte administration launched a crackdown against ABS-CBN and Bulatlat. He also has ties with a big fishing company.

items: Gamaliel Asis Cordoba was appointed as the third associate justice of the Supreme Court by President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. in November 2023, following his tenure as chairperson of the Commission on Audit (COA).

During his time at COA, Cordoba oversaw significant financial audits, including the disallowance of confidential funds for Vice President Sara Duterte's office, and faced criticism for delays in publishing Annual Audit Reports.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
Gamaliel Asis Cordoba entered President Ferdinand Marcos Jr.’s administration in 2022 when Commission on Audit (COA) chairperson Jose Calida resigned just months into his post.

On November 13, Cordoba’s strong ties with Marcos became apparent again after the President picked him as his third appointee to the Supreme Court (SC). Cordoba replaced former associate justice Amy Lazaro Javier, an appointee of former president Rodrigo Duterte, who retired on November 16.

He is the latest Marcos appointee to the High Court after Associate Justice Raul Villanueva in 2025, and recently, Chief Justice Rodil Zalameda on November 5. He is the country’s 196th SC associate justice.

This brings the number of Marcos appointees to the High Court to three, compared with two appointed by the late former president Benigno Aquino III and nine by former president Rodrigo Duterte. Zalameda’s appointment as chief justice leaves another vacancy in the associate justice post.

Cordoba served for four years and a month in COA, the government institution mandated to audit government finances and purchases. In 2022 and 2023, he was external auditor of the International Labour Organization.

Under Cordoba, COA issued a notice of disallowance on Vice President Sara Duterte’s P73-million confidential funds for the Office of the Vice President (OVP), and P75 million for the Department of Education (DepEd)
While COA has already cleared the DepEd funds, it affirmed with finality the disallowance against the OVP. (READ: With finality: COA affirms disallowance of Sara Duterte’s P73-M confidential funds)

It was also under Cordoba in 2024 when the commission started delaying the publication of its Annual Audit Reports or AAR. Budget transparency advocates, journalists, and even politicians rely on AARs to check how agencies used their funds and if there are red flags from these transactions.
Advocates criticized the delay in publication, asserting that it neither indicated transparency nor established credibility.

blocks.caption: COA delays publishing of audit reports. How can this affect us?

blocks.text: Cordoba was the longest serving commissioner of the National Telecommunications Commission (NTC) — from 2009 to 2022.
He was the NTC commissioner when former president Duterte waged a campaign against media giant ABS-CBN that ultimately led to the network’s shutdown.

At the height of the controversy, Cordoba said in one of the legislative inquiries in 2020 that the NTC would “most likely” issue a provisional authority so ABS-CBN could continue operating pending a franchise renewal. Cordoba also said at the time that ABS-CBN had no standing penalties with the NTC.
But ABS-CBN’s franchise expired and was not renewed during Duterte’s term. Its shutdown led to the retrenchment of around 5,000 personnel.
When Cordoba was still with the NTC, the website of alternative news site Bulatlat was also blocked.

Before the end of Duterte’s term in 2022, then-national security adviser Hermogenes Esperon Jr. wrote to Cordoba, requesting the commission to “order Philippine Internet Service Providers (ISPs) to block access to the following websites affiliated [with] and are supporting these terrorists and terrorist organizations.”
Esperon used the highly contested anti-terror law to justify the request. He also cited affiliations with terrorist organizations without providing substantial evidence.
After a legal battle, Bulatlat’s website was unblocked after the news site won against the NTC and Esperon in court.
But this was not the only issue that Cordoba got embroiled in.

A Rappler investigation in 2024 showed that the family of Cordoba’s wife, Monica Elena Cordoba, partly owns the commercial fishing company Mercidar Fishing Corporation. A copy of Cordoba’s 2023 Statement of Assets, Liabilities, and Net Worth obtained by Rappler showed that he was also a shareholder of Mercidar in 2015 and 2019 — the years when he was already with the NTC.

To avoid conflicts of interest, Section 9 of the Code of Conduct for Public Officials requires officials to divest themselves of their shareholdings or financial interest within 60 days of taking office. Rappler found that during Cordoba’s time in the NTC, the commission stopped issuing service numbers for trackers that would prevent unregulated fishing.
Mercidar is central to the municipal waters issue. Originally, 15-kilometer municipal waters were exclusively for small fisherfolk.

But in December 2023, Malabon City Regional Trial Court Judge Zaldy Docena allowed Mercidar to operate within the 15-kilometer municipal waters except in shallow waters (less than 7 fathoms deep). A year later, in 2024, the SC affirmed this decision.

blocks.caption: Top officials with private interests spoil effort to track big fishers

blocks.text: Although not a politician, Cordoba has proven to be somewhat of a political survivor, having served under four presidents: Gloria Macapagal Arroyo, Aquino, Duterte, and Marcos.
Arroyo appointed him in 2009, and the succeeding presidents kept him as part of their administrations until his appointment to the COA, an independent body.

His COA profile claimed that Cordoba’s stint in the NTC saw the improvement in the country’s internet connectivity. It also said that under him, the NTC broke the long-time duopoly in the country’s telecommunications industry.

“The country’s fixed broadband and mobile internet speeds remarkably improved globally under his leadership with Ookla Speedtest Global Index now ranking the Philippines 41st out of 180 countries globally for fixed broadband and 79th out of 140 countries for mobile,” said Cordoba’s profile.

“… The NTC broke the long-time duopoly in the telecommunications industry by successfully selecting a third telco through a most transparent bidding process under the guidance of the International Telecommunication Union,” it added.
Cordoba is a government official through and through. In 2010, Arroyo gave him the Presidential Medal of Merit “for his exemplary performance and service delivery to the Filipino people.”
He has also held the following positions in government:

items: director of the Office of Presidential Chief of Staff (2001-2002)
assistant executive secretary (2002-2003)
undersecretary, Office of the President (2003-2006)
appointments secretary, Office of the President (2006-2007)
member of board of directors, Philippine Amusement and Gaming Corporation (2008-2009)

blocks.text: Before joining government, Cordoba worked as an associate lawyer at Siguion Reyna, Montecillo and Ongsiako Law Offices. He also worked as a tax lawyer at accounting firm SyCip Gorres Velayo and Co.

The new SC associate justice joined the long list of High Court magistrates who are products of the Ateneo de Manila University. He earned his economics degree from the university in 1992, then his juris doctor four years later. Cordoba passed the Bar in 1997 with Roll No. 42213.
Like Zalameda, Cordoba is a member of the Fraternal Order of Utopia.

blocks.caption: What will Gamaliel Cordoba, Marcos’ newest SC pick, bring to Padre Faura?

blocks.text: To secure his SC appointment, Cordoba had to beat other strong contenders.

Some of the shortlisted nominees for the post have been serving in the judiciary for decades, or are respected lawyers like Solicitor General Darlene Marie Berberabe, whom Marcos did not pick in the last two selections for SC justice.
Cordoba applied only once and got the job.

blocks.caption: Who are the candidates short-listed for SC associate justice?

blocks.text: During his Judicial and Bar Council interview on October 13, Cordoba said he applied for the position because he felt like it was the “time” to seek higher office. He said he believed it was his chance to affect more people and have a lasting legacy in public service.

Given his experience with mainly executive offices, the new justice said he would bring to the SC en banc a different perspective in handling cases. He said he believed that while having judicial experience was an advantage for an associate justice, his executive experience was something that should be considered too.
“We’re bringing many facets and many fresh new ideas which we can inject into the decisions,” he said.

As an associate justice, Cordoba promised to support the SC’s Strategic Plan for Judicial Innovations or SPJI. He said the program has to continue and be expanded even more, adding that the initiative brings the courts closer to people.
SPJI is the brainchild of former chief justice Alexander Gesmundo that introduced innovations in the judiciary, including digitalization. The project has been running since 2022 and will end in 2027.

blocks.caption: What will Gamaliel Cordoba, Marcos’ newest SC pick, bring to Padre Faura?

blocks.text: As an SC justice, Cordoba said he would be the type who would follow what’s written in the 1987 Constitution and existing jurisprudence. He said he would act according to the Code of Judicial Conduct and Accountability.
Cordoba also said he would inhibit himself if cases he participated in under the NTC, COA, and related offices found their way to the Supreme Court. – Rappler.com

articles.title: Hi-tech Shenzhen takes centre stage as Xi sends ‘Chinamaxxing’ message at Apec summit
articles.summary:
Host city offers showcase of China’s rise into a confident and innovative power central to global economy

In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of…

blocks.text: In a Shenzhen square on a balmy evening, locals and tourists watched the dozens of glinting towers that make up the city’s skyline ripple through the colour spectrum – cyan and violet, cyber green, China’s national scarlet and gold – repeatedly flashing the words “Apec 2026”.
The Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit is a dream showcase for one of China’s most advanced cities, and the country’s leader, Xi Jinping, is basking in its neon glow.

On the sidelines, a series of high-profile bilateral meetings and the announcement of a historic three-way summit with Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin have cemented Xi’s status as an agenda setter on the global stage.

The broader Apec summit, meanwhile, provides an opportunity for China to present itself as a steward of multilateralism against what it terms “unilateralism and protectionism” – that is to say, trade measures taken against Beijing by countries such as the US.

blocks.caption: A humanoid robot serves a cup of coffee at the Apec media centre in Shenzhen. Photograph: Tingshu Wang/Reuters

blocks.text: All this is set against the futuristic backdrop that is Shenzhen, a city that perhaps better than no other embodies China’s rise into a confident, technologically innovative power central to the global economy.
A photo display in the Apec media centre charts Shenzhen’s transformation from sparsely populated marshland, calling it “a miracle in the history of world development created by the Chinese people”.

“[Xi] wants people to go home Chinamaxxing,” said Prof Astrid Nordin, of King’s College London. “Shenzhen is itself part of the message. It’s a showcase of Chinese technological and economic achievements, and of China’s claim that it offers opportunities for prosperity in a world increasingly characterised by uncertainty and conflict.”

blocks.caption: A light show in Shenzhen on Sunday. Photograph: VCG/Getty Images

blocks.text: Like the light show, the summit is being carefully coordinated. The Financial Times cited people familiar with the matter as saying it would be one of the most tightly controlled in the organisation’s history, with leaders having to travel to a state guesthouse beside Shenzhen’s tiger safari park to meet Xi. The paper said diplomats had grumbled that the format “seems designed to reduce the free-flowing discussion characteristic of prior editions”.
Setting out its expectations for the summit, China’s foreign ministry has said it looks forward to “practical results in key areas such as trade, connectivity, digital economy, AI and so on”.

Already, Xi has announced trade wins with Canada’s Mark Carney, extending remission measures for certain Chinese steel and aluminium products by two years in exchange for tariff relief on Canadian pork, fish and seafood exports.

blocks.caption: Mark Carney and Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on Tuesday. Photograph: Adrian Wyld/The Canadian Press/AP

blocks.text: A meeting with Papua New ⁠Guinea’s leader, meanwhile, showed how Beijing’s geopolitical priorities have been absorbed and reflected by its allies, with James Marape recounting to Xi how he had closed Taiwan’s office in his country despite domestic challenges in doing so.

The most important meeting will be between Xi and Trump. The leaders of the world’s two superpowers are expected to tackle a broad range of issues including AI and trade. In a move that could strain the fragile tariff truce that the two leaders first agreed last year, the Trump administration said on Monday it would further restrict China’s access to advanced AI chips.

Christopher Adams, a senior adviser at the law firm Covington who was at the centre of trade negotiations with China for the Obama and first Trump administrations, said: “The trade truce may increasingly look like a ceasefire in a war where major combat operations remain on hold but skirmishes are escalating to the point where the line between peace and war is blurred.
“I don’t see pressure to announce a further extension of the trade truce in Shenzhen. If a significant extension is announced, that would be an upside surprise.”

blocks.caption: Xi and Donald Trump at the White House in September. Photograph: Abaca/Shutterstock

blocks.text: China has not hesitated to leverage Apec’s multinational platform in service of its arguments. A commentary by the state news agency Xinhua on Tuesday said: “Amid deepening geopolitical rivalries and growing global divisions, [China’s hosting] sends a clear signal that great-power competition need not be a zero-sum game, and that one country’s development need not come at the expense of another.”

The chair of the Apec senior officials’ meeting, Chen Xu, said Beijing had made trade “openness” a key focus of its Apec year and looked forward to “achieving more practical outcomes on the trade front”.

The much anticipated trilateral summit with Trump and Putin, on the other hand, could prove largely symbolic. For Xi, “it provides the appearance of China shaping the world order as an equal to the United States,” said Dr Kevork Oskanian, an expert on Russia at the University of Exeter. “Agreement on substantial issues, which would, in any case, require extensive preparatory negotiations, is unlikely.”

blocks.caption: Nesting dolls depicting Xi, Trump and Vladimir Putin in a gift shop in Moscow. Photograph: Igor Ivanko/AFP/Getty Images

blocks.text: For China’s ruling Communist party, the political pomp has another key purpose. Nordin said summits were “occasions for leaders to tell stories about the world, about their country’s place in it … and one of the most important audiences for those stories is at home.”

For the locals watching the skyscraper light show on Monday night, the symbolism was not lost. China’s export might had helped it become increasingly powerful on the world stage, said one local man, who did not give his name. “It’s so great that the summit will take place in Shenzhen,” he said. “I feel very proud.”
